clubs.description: Alpha Kappa Lambda (ΑΚΛ) is an American collegiate social fraternity for men founded at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1914. Today, it operates 23 active chapters and colonies and over 27,000 initiated members. Alpha Kappa Lambda was founded on April 22, 1914 by a group of young men attending the University of California, Berkeley. Its birth, however, dates back to 1906 when a group of friends discussed the "need of Christian men for a place to live and study that was within their (financial) means." After assisting in the cleanup of the Great 1906 San Francisco Earthquake, four students re-addressed their desire to organize a house club during a YMCA conference in Pacific Grove, California. It was decided to form "Los Amigos" in 1907, which was a house club named from the Spanish translation of "The Friends." Shortly after, seven more men joined Los Amigos. Reverend Gail Cleland, one of the original eleven members of Los Amigos, recalled, "When we organized Los Amigos as a house club, house clubs and fraternities were dime a dozen. They came, they lived for a few months or a few years, then they went out of existence again. But Los Amigos did not go

clubs.summary: Realize Your Potential. The mission of Alpha Xi Delta is to enrich the life of every Alpha Xi Delta. We will nurture unity and cooperation, foster intellectual, professional and personal growth, exemplify the highest ethical conduct, and more.
clubs.description: We are a Panhellenic sorority founded in 1893 at Lombard College as one of the oldest women's fraternities and established/recognized by Penn State University in 1942. We are a close-knit sisterhood of women committed to upholding our core values of sisterhood, knowledge, leadership, and service. Our National philanthropy is the Kindly Hearts Initiative which provides support, funds, and advocacy for children and teens experiencing foster care.

clubs.name: Alpha Zeta at University Park
clubs.summary: Alpha Zeta is an Honorary, Professional, Co-ed, Agriculture based Fraternity
clubs.description: Founded nationally in 1897 and Established on the Penn State campus in 1898, Alpha Zeta is the original agricultural interest fraternity on campus and in the nation. Our house, located next to Rec Hall and across from Waring Commons at 360 N Burrowes St was completed in 1915, making it the second oldest fraternity house on campus. Our founding members had a significant influence on shaping the Farmer's High School of Pennsylvania into what we now know as The Pennsylvania State University. This is evident around the campus in the historic plaques and by the names of the buildings. Alpha Zeta is a member of the Interfraternity Council and participates in all IFC programs, events, and standards. Alpha Zeta has continually achieved noteworthy rankings in both IFC and university-facilitated Standards of Excellence metrics. We are always looking for men and women to share our interest in agriculture and related fields, if you think you may be interested, please stop by the house or contact us! Jacob Straw President, The Morrill Chapter of Alpha Zeta

clubs.summary: The Alternative Dispute Resolution Program (ADR) serves as the principal ADR organization in the Law School. Its purpose is to help develop the communication and problem-solving skills necessary to be a successful lawyer and advocate.
clubs.description: The Alternative Dispute Resolution Program (ADR) serves as the principal ADR organization at Penn State Dickinson School of Law. Its purpose is to help develop the communication and problem-solving skills necessary to be a successful lawyer and advocate. This is done through preparing student members to compete in ADR competition across the country and internationally in topics such as negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and client counseling. The Alternative Dispute Resolution Program is run entirely by students; members are selected annually through a competition held at the start of the fall semester

clubs.name: Alzheimer's Buddies at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: A student-led organization aimed to overcome the social disengagement experienced by those with Alzheimer’s Disease by pairing student volunteers 1-to-1 with dementia residents.
clubs.description: Loneliness and isolation are common psychological symptoms prevalent in individuals suffering from intermediate-to-late-stages of Alzheimer's Disease. To alleviate these symptoms, students at Penn State have joined to form the Alzheimer's Buddies at Penn State, a chapter of a national organization where student volunteers are paired 1-to-1 with dementia residents at Juniper Village, a senior care facility in State College. These students meet weekly with their buddies, forming new bonds and lasting relationships with those suffering from the terrible disorder. Additionally, the Alzheimer's Buddies at Penn State are committed to spreading awareness about Alzheimer's Disease by participating in and hosting fundraisers, as well as hosting talks on current advancements in Alzheimer's Disease research.

clubs.name: Alzheimer’s Awareness Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Alzheimer's Awareness Club aims to raise awareness for Alzheimer's and dementia and to support research, advocate for improved healthcare services, and provide resources for those navigating the challenges of Alzheimer's
clubs.description: The goal of the Alzheimer's Awareness Club is to raise awareness and promote understanding of Alzheimer's and dementia within the community. Through fundraisers, donation drives, volunteer work, and outreach initiatives this organization will help families who have been impacted by this disease. This organization also advocates for improving brain health early on to avoid Alzheimer's and dementia in the future.

clubs.name: American Association of Drilling Engineers at University Park
clubs.summary: The American Association of Drilling Engineers is a professional society with the purpose of gaining energy industry exposure for its members. This is pursued with technical electives, technical discussions, and tours of oil and natural gas rigs.
clubs.description: The American Association of Drilling Engineers is a professional society with the purpose of gaining energy industry exposure for its members. This is pursued with technical electives, technical discussions, tours of oil and natural gas rigs and facilities, and our annual trip to the AADE conference. Technical electives allow for an industry professional to teach a weekend course to students about a currently used engineering technique. Our technical discussions allow for students to view the newest technology of the oil industry be presented and discussed by current engineers. Our rig tours allow for students to tour and interview workers within working facilities of the energy industry. Our conference allows for the most dedicated members to talk with hundreds of companies directly.

clubs.name: American Association of University Women at Penn State World Campus
clubs.summary: AAUW at Penn State World Campus is a student-led community dedicated to educating and empowering women, girls and marginalized genders. We work to develop leadership skills, build confidence, and connect with changemakers and leaders around the world.
clubs.description: AAUW at Penn State World Campus is a student-led chapter of the American Association of University Women (AAUW), dedicated to advancing equity for women and girls. Through advocacy, leadership development, educational programs, and meaningful conversations, our organization empowers members to drive positive change on campus and in our communities. We offer access to national resources, leadership opportunities, and initiatives such as salary negotiation training, Title IX advocacy, and confidence-building workshops. AAUW at Penn State WC is open to all students who support our mission, with a welcoming, inclusive culture and a focus on impact. Whether you’re passionate about gender equity, looking to connect with a community of changemakers, or want to develop your leadership skills, we welcome you to join us in creating a more just and equitable world.

clubs.name: American Constitution Society at Dickinson Law in Carlisle
clubs.summary: The American Constitution Society (ACS) is the nation’s foremost progressive legal organization, focusing on promoting civil rights, progressive values, and training the next generation of advocates. Our local chapter supports these efforts in Carlisle.
clubs.description: The American Constitution Society for Law and Policy (ACS) is the nation's foremost progressive legal organization, with a diverse nationwide network that includes nearly 250 student and lawyer chapters, and progressive lawyers, students, judges, scholars, elected officials, and advocates. Our mission is to support and advocate for laws and legal systems that redress the founding failures of our Constitution, strengthen our democratic legitimacy, uphold the rule of law, and realize the promise of equality for all, including people of color, women, LGBTQ+ people, people with disabilities, and other historically excluded communities.

We also seek to promote technical excellence and a collaborative community between our members and the Aerospace faculty at Penn State. Our chapter participates in many events, such as field trips, design challenges, guest speakers, and involvement fairs. Our chapter tries to pick events that are both rewarding and inspiring for our members. We also try and pick events that help underclassmen determine their choice of major. We hope to be a place where undecided students can learn whether they want to be an aerospace engineer. Our chapter also promotes the national organization. Each year, we participate in the AIAA Region 1 Student Research Conference. Finally, our chapter tries to participate in science-related events in the State College community. We do this to try and increase the interest in STEM fields among students in our community.

clubs.name: American Medical Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: AMSA is an academic and professional development organization for students interested in attending medical or PA school. Meetings feature guest speakers, networking events, and application help sessions.
clubs.description: AMSA is a student-governed, national organization committed to representing the concerns of physicians-in-training. AMSA members are medical students, premedical students, interns, residents and practicing physicians. How is AMSA different from other organizations? When you join AMSA, you become part of a vital force of future physicians who believe that patients and health professionals are partners in the management of health care and that access to high-quality health care is a right and not a privilege. At AMSA, activism is a way of life. Student idealism is transformed into meaningful public service, innovation and institutional change.

clubs.name: American Medical Women's Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The AMWA's goal is to advocate for equity and excellence in healthcare, advancing women in medicine. With values of mentorship, equity, diversity, integrity, inclusion, and collaboration, the AMWA aims to support female physicians and pre-med students.
clubs.description: For more than a hundred years, the American Medical Women's Association (AMWA) has dedicated itself to promoting the progression of women in the field of medicine. Despite a significant increase in the number of women pursuing careers in medicine, there has not been a proportional rise in women attaining top leadership roles. AMWA aims to bridge this gender gap in leadership by focusing on advocacy, mentorship, leadership training, research, community building, and policy changes. Its ultimate objective is to bring about institutional and cultural changes that ensure gender equity and equal career opportunities for women in medicine. As a premedical division, the AMWA provides members countless benefits, resources, information, and opportunities to strengthen their application to medical school. Additionally, premedical divisions allow the upcoming generation of physicians to work towards the important changes they would like to see in the field of medicine. Finally, being apart of the AMWA can continue throughout your entire career as a physician, with applicable benefits throughout each stage.

clubs.description: ASTA is a student-run organization that is meant to support and uplift its members by serving their unique needs. Whether you are just being introduced to string instruments or have been playing for decades, there is a place for you to learn and grow in ASTA. As an official chapter of our national organization, our members receive benefits such as teaching resources, professional education, local and national events, a career center, insurance programs, and access to a vibrant and collaborative strings community. Our organization also regularly welcomes guest speakers and travels to attend the ASTA conference in February. Join us in learning more about how to teach the next generation of string players!

On Fridays/Saturdays, we frequent game night tournaments and movies screenings. Feel free to email us or DM on Insta for any questions or to be added to the listerv! :)

clubs.name: Anime Organization at University Park
clubs.summary: The Penn State Anime Organization (PSAO) will sponsor events promoting the understanding and enjoyment of the Japanese art forms of anime (Japanese Animation), manga (Japanese comics), and anime associated video games.
clubs.description: Since September 2001, the PSAO has been bringing anime, manga and Japanese pop culture to the University Park campus. Working to provide both weekly screenings and a social environment for Penn State's anime/manga fan base, the PSAO is continually broadening its horizons. The PSAO meetings serve multiple functions, on Wednesdays we meet at 7:00 pm in various locations for rotating social activities, which we call our Manga Nights. On Tuesdays, we alternate between Viewing Nights, where we watch a variety of anime as a group, and Gaming Nights, where we play anime-related and Japanese games. We also hold two parties a semester: Halloween and Winter Formal in the Fall semester and Valentine's and Spring Fling in the Spring semester. Additionally, we offer a way for students to attend some anime conventions, one of which was founded by us! For more details about our events, please check out the PSAO discord: https://discord.com/invite/aq3Y9SV Our organization is made up of a very diverse group of students; the club executives and members bring together interests, majors, and personalities of all types to create an engaging and fun club environment.

clubs.description: There are four specific purposes of AGSA. First, AGSA raises money for graduate students to travel to professional meetings. Second, AGSA serves as an information center for concerns related to anthropology graduate student life, such as curriculum and funding, especially for incoming students. Third, AGSA serves as a liaison between the anthropology graduate students and anthropology faculty. Fourth, AGSA is dedicated to public outreach and education about anthropology.

ASA also seeks to remain informed about current issues affecting Armenians worldwide and to maintain strong ties with Armenian Student Associations and the broader Armenian community.

clubs.name: Biotechnology and Pharmaceutical Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The PSU Biotech and Pharmaceutical Club connects industry and students. We are committed to the personal and professional growth of our members. By providing education, skills, and networking opportunities to enhance exposure to the healthcare field.
clubs.description: The PSU Biotech and Pharmaceutical club is a student run organization with the mission to connect industry and the students of Happy Valley. We are committed to cultivating the personal and professional growth of our members. We put a priority on providing education, skills and networking opportunities to enhance exposure within the healthcare field. We work to develop relationships and strengthen existing interactions with academia, pharma, and biotech companies. With the goal making Penn State a recruiting ground for the biotech and pharma industry. We cover Finance, Supply Chain, Marketing, Advertising, Sales, Health Care Consulting, and R&D. Students can expect to learn about each of these fields while progressing professionally and exploring different career paths.

clubs.name: Birding Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Join the Penn State Bird Club to discover your local birds! From campus to Rothrock State Forest, and beyond! We explore, learn, and conserve our feathered friends. All students and skill levels are welcome, we have binoculars to borrow! 🐦 #BirdingPSU
clubs.description: Welcome to the Penn State Bird Club, where we're all about spreading our wings and connecting students to the incredible world of birds right in our backyard. Whether you're a seasoned birder or just starting to explore the avian wonders around us, there's a perch for you in our flock. At the Penn State Bird Club, we're not just about admiring birds from afar – we're all about getting up close and personal with the feathered friends that call Happy Valley home. From the iconic American robin to the elusive Eastern screech owl, our region is teeming with diverse bird species waiting to be discovered. Join us for birdwatching outings to local hotspots like Rothrock State Forest, Shaver's Creek Environmental Center, and the beautiful arboretum right on campus. Our experienced birders will guide you through the sights and sounds of the natural world, helping you hone your identification skills and deepen your appreciation for our avian neighbors. But the Penn State Bird Club isn't just about birdwatching – it's also a community of like-minded individuals passionate about conservation and environmental stewardship. Get involved in our outreach and education initiatives, wher

clubs.name: Black Emotions Advocate Team at University Park
clubs.summary: Our goal as an organization is to create a safe space for students to seek mental health advice, help, and resources from students that look like them and share similar experiences.
clubs.description: "The Beat" is a dedicated organization focused on addressing the mental health needs of Black students on campus. Our primary aim is to establish a supportive and inclusive environment where Black students can freely seek guidance, support, and resources related to mental health. By fostering connections with on-campus resources, we strive to provide Black students with access to professional support services, counseling, and mental health resources tailored to their specific needs and experiences. Through advocacy, outreach, and collaboration with university resources, we aim to promote mental wellness, resilience, and empowerment among Black students, ultimately fostering a community where mental health is prioritized and supported.

clubs.description: BLSA at Penn State Dickinson Law serves as the leading advocate for black law students and is dedicated to the development of talented, involved black attorneys. Founded in 1968, the National Black Law Students Association (NBLSA), was formed to promote the needs and goals of black law students and effect change in the legal community. The largest entirely student run organization in the United States with nearly 6,000 members, NBLSA is also comprised of chapters or affiliates in six different countries including The Bahamas, Nigeria, and South Africa.

clubs.name: Black Law Students Association at Dickinson Law in Carlisle
clubs.summary: Black Law Students Association at Dickinson Law (Carlisle)

BLSA promotes the welfare of its members through educational, professional, cultural and social programs. It also provides a forum for the discussion of local and national issues affecting both the Black law student community and the University community as a whole.

clubs.name: Black Male Leadership Symposium at University Park

clubs.description: The Black Male Leadership Symposium aims to foster unity and stability among black males; however, we welcome all men despite their race, sexuality, religious background, creed, etc. We actively engage in retention and recruitment efforts. Our organization facilitates personal and professional development through professional workshops with corporate sponsors. We also collaborate with various student organizations on campus to enhance connections among African American men. Our commitment to promoting diversity at Penn State involves spearheading and supporting initiatives that encourage growth in the African American population. We work closely with the Office of Diversity & Enhancement Programs and Smeal faculty and staff to achieve these goals.

clubs.name: Black Muslim Initiative at University Park

clubs.name: Black Women In Tech at University Park
clubs.summary: Empowering Black Women in Tech at Penn State
clubs.description: Black Women in Tech is a student organization at Penn State dedicated to fostering a supportive and inclusive community that empowers Black women in technology, while also welcoming and supporting other underrepresented women of color. We strive to create a space where members can share their experiences, access valuable resources, and grow both academically and professionally in a field where their representation is often lacking.

clubs.name: BLK Elites Dance Company at University Park
clubs.summary: Blk Elites was created to provide a space of innovation and service for the Black community through dance. Blk Elites, where talent meets culture. We are black, we are love, and we are beauty, WE ARE BLK Elites.

clubs.description: BLK Men in Tech: Penn State Chapter is a welcoming and inclusive organization that celebrates and uplifts the Black experience in the world of technology. Our mission is to empower individuals by providing the mentorship, resources, and community support needed to successfully navigate and excel in their tech careers. We strive to create a space where everyone feels valued, respected, and inspired to reach their full potential. Through accessible opportunities, collaborative events, and meaningful connections, we aim to break down barriers and ensure that no one has to navigate the journey alone. Whether you're just beginning to explore the tech field or are seeking guidance to grow and advance your career, BLK Men in Tech is here to help you succeed—because your journey matters, and together, we rise.

clubs.name: Block and Bridle Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Promoting a higher scholastic standard, PSU's Block and Bridle is the premier livestock and horse club on campus. Our members come from a variety of backgrounds and majors but have one thing in common - a true advocacy and love for the animal science.
clubs.description: Block and Bridle, known as the premier livestock and horse club on campus at Penn State, is one of the most active clubs on campus, not just on Ag Hill but also at the university level. Block and Bridle currently has 75 active members, these members have livestock and horses as a common interest and participate in a variety of activities which range from social and educational events to community service. Transfer and freshmen students are greeted in the fall at the club's Welcome Back picnic where old members reunite and new members begin to form lasting friendships. General club meetings are held every first and third Thursday of the month, with the board of directors meetings being held on alternative weeks. New students have ample opportunities to become involved with the club and are encouraged to participate as they are required to assist with at least four events to become an initiated member. The diverse background of club members allows the interests in all species of livestock to be well represented at club events. clubs.name: Blooms and Shrooms at University Park

clubs.description: Blooms & Shrooms is an undergraduate mycology and plant pathology club that is for anyone who is interested in fungi, mushrooms, plant diseases, or just appreciating nature! As a club we take engage in mushroom forays on and off campus, learn about topics in mycology, and engage with researchers working with fungi. We pride ourselves on being open and welcoming to all, so please reach out or stop in if you're interested: no prior experience necessary. Please reach out to Poncho (czm6098@psu.edu) or Allison (acw5890@psu.edu) for information regarding meeting times/locations and joining the club GroupMe.

With plenty of leadership opportunities available and plenty of ways to get involved, the Blue & White Society is University Park's most active student organization. To learn more, check out our website at http://www.bluewhitesociety.com/. Our Mission: To enhance student life at Penn State through diversified experience, with an emphasis on service to the community, civic leadership, tradition, and outreach while establishing the foundation of a lifelong commitment to the University as members of the Penn State Alumni Association.

Nonetheless, this club will function as a cooperative proto-public in that all members are equally responsible and accountable for each others' development. A bodybuilder, above all, is someone who stays disciplined. Respect and discipline are vital building blocks of physical and mental well-being.

The organization combines the strengths of the former Bodybuilding and Fitness Club and Girl Gains, creating one inclusive community dedicated to making fitness accessible, empowering, and enjoyable for everyone. Members have opportunities to learn about safe and effective training techniques, nutrition, recovery, goal setting, and healthy lifestyle habits while building friendships with others who share similar interests. Our club hosts workouts, educational workshops, guest speakers, social events, and fitness-related activities that help members develop confidence both inside and outside the gym. clubs.description: Book Club is a casual social organization for both undergraduate and graduate to engage in discussion over shared reading experiences. If you're looking for an informal, low-key-but-fun environment in which to discuss stories, other media, and life in general, this is the group for you. Through weekly in-person meetings, book-based social events, and engaging discussions, we help forge connections between those students who might otherwise have stayed inside reading. All are welcome, and books are chosen by voting on member suggestions. Please email Secretary Kayleigh McLaughlin at kam8570@psu.edu or President Adam Basile acb6443@psu.edu for more information, or to be added to the club GroupMe. We'd love to have you!

clubs.summary: The purpose of the Bounce Dance Organization is to gather students who are passionate about street dance and organize dance-related activities.
clubs.description: Hi everyone!! Welcome to Bounce! We are a BIG family that welcomes everyone as long as you have a passion for dancing. (The best thing is you don't need to have experience for it.) We were established in 2015, and we are the FIRST recognized Asian dance organization. We provide a variety of dance styles and many performance opportunities. We have performed over 200 dance pieces in various styles, including Hip Hop, Jazz, Heels, Urban, K-pop, Contemporary, and Dancehall. We also have our own YouTube channel, which offers dancers more opportunities to showcase their talents. We also hold open workshops for beginners. Please join us if you are interested! :)

clubs.name: Boxing Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Promotes the physical well being of the Penn State community and provides instruction for recreational and competitive skills in boxing.
clubs.description: The Penn State Boxing Club promotes the physical well being of the Penn State community and provides instruction for recreational and competitive skills in boxing. No prior experience is required; we have trained side by side with first-timers, skilled fighters, and national collegiate champions. The Club offers two different levels of boxing, the introductory club team, and the competitive level team. In the introductory club level students are given the space and instruction to learn the fundamentals of boxing while improving their physical fitness under the coaching of experienced competitive team members. On the competitive team, for which their is a semesterly try-out, students are given the opportunity to represent Penn State on a regional and national inter-collegiate level within the National Collegiate Boxing Association. Competitive team members are expected to train more frequently and become members of USA boxing as is required for all competing boxers nationwide.

clubs.name: Branch of the American Meteorological Society at University Park
clubs.summary: Fosters interest in meteorology and to serve as a professional, service, and social organization for Penn State meteorology students as a local chapter of the American Meteorology Society.
clubs.description: The Pennsylvania State University Branch of the American Meteorological Society and Chapter of the National Weather Association (PSUBAMS(CNWA)) provides meteorology students at Penn State informative and beneficial opportunities to gain knowledge of the meteorological community. To highlight the various aspects of meteorology, PSUBAMS takes advantage of speakers and events associated with areas such as private industry, government, academia, broadcast and communication, and weather risk management. PSUBAMS speakers provide realism and foresight to Penn State meteorology students striving to supplement classroom learning with real world advice. PSUBAMS ("The ‘P' is silent!") is an official student chapter of both the AMS and NWA. This partnership with the two premier meteorological organizations allows us to work with them when organizing important events, most notably the AMS and NWA Conferences. In addition, our affiliations allow members many additional opportunities for scholarships and recruitment sessions. Around the department, PSUBAMS generally holds meetings a few times per month. We welcome in speakers from all across the meteorological community, including AccuWeath

clubs.description: We are a national student-led movement trying to end political polarization on college campuses. Our goal is to encourage students to engage differing beliefs, experiences and perspectives through hosting open discussions, debates and guest speaker events. My e-board and I plan to host both informational and leisure events such as discussions on reproductive rights and immigration policies, and debates on whether pineapple belongs on pizza or which brand is better: Nike or Jordan. We are not here to change minds or create centrists but to find a middle ground where all mindsets and beliefs can co-exist.

Founder Resources: From technical "war rooms" to cloud credits and hardware, we provide the infrastructure needed to turn MVPs into scalable startups. The Network: Members gain access to a curated pipeline of alumni founders and mentors who have successfully navigated the transition from campus builder to industry leader. clubs.name: Club Cross Country at University Park
clubs.summary: Cross Country was founded so runners of all abilities could have the chance to train and compete in distance running at the collegiate level without the stresses of a varsity sport.
clubs.description: This club is open to all types of runners! Whether you're just here to meet people and stay in shape, or you want to continue competitive racing in college, we'd be happy to have you. The club gives students an opportunity to compete with other running clubs and varsity teams in the region during the cross country, indoor track, and outdoor track seasons. Each year our cross country and track seasons culminate with trips to NIRCA Nationals, where we often place well both as individuals and teams. But racing is not mandatory, and our good times can be found on and off the course! Whether it's a picnic at Sunset Park, a THON fundraiser, a fun run, or a post-practice game of frisbee, Club XC always has something exciting going on. If you're looking to be a part of a close-knit group that supports each other, values positivity, digs deep, and has fun, look no further! We practice every weekday at 4:30pm at Rec Hall. (4:00pm during winter time change) No practice is mandatory. Come as frequently as you'd like! We offer multiple different run options every day and you are free to run at whatever pace fits your training. With so many people on our team, there is always a group to run with

clubs.name: Club Curling at University Park
clubs.summary: Penn State Club Curling (PSCC) is PSU's newest addition to the Club Sports program. PSCC competes against other universities within USA College Curling. We proudly host the largest college curling team in America, with over 20 registered curlers.
clubs.description: Penn State Club Curling was founded originally as Curling at Penn State in 2018. In 2023, Curling at Penn State split into two organizations: Penn State Club Curling (PSCC) and Nittany Recreational Curling League (NRCL). PSCC represents the competition team that travels across the United States to play in the USA College Curling circuit, a branch of USA Curling. With over 20 members, we represent the largest group of college curlers in the United States. PSCC has competed at three national championships (2022, 2023, 2024) and has qualified for four (including the cancelled 2020 Nationals). In both 2022 and 2024, Penn State won the esteemed "Spirit of Curling" Award at Nationals in recognition of outstanding skill and sportsmanship in the sport. In 2024, Penn State ended the regular season as #1 in America via the college rankings. PSCC frequently travels for collegiate-level bonspiels during the academic year. The typical competition season runs October-March, with the potential for competing in smaller events in the later spring. During the 2023-2024, we competed in 68 games (draws) across all bonspiels! We frequently send multiple teams to events, so there are plenty of opportuni

clubs.name: Club Dressage at University Park
clubs.summary: To promote horsemanship by teaching good sound quality basics and introducing students to the classical riding/training principles of Dressage.
clubs.description: PSU Dressage is a club sports team that competes in the Intercollegiate Dressage Association (IDA). Our diverse team is made up of enthusiastic people from all majors, ages, backgrounds, and experiences. From international riders to first-time riders our team welcomes and caters everyone. If you are passionate and dedicated, and looking for a well-rounded experience -- riding, socials, community service and more -- this is the team for you! Simply said, dressage is a style of riding that does not include jumping, but is referred to by many as "horse-dancing." If dictionary definitions are more your speed, dressage (ˈdresäZH/) is a noun meaning "the art of riding and training a horse in a manner that develops obedience, flexibility, and balance." Nevertheless, dressage is the foundation for most types of riding, so if you're looking to start riding or strengthen your riding, joining our team is a step in the right direction. We learn and train with our coach, Lindsay Hafer (check out "meet your team" for her bio), at an eventing barn called Standing Ovation in Port Matilda. There we have the privilege of teaming up with over 20 horses who prepare us for our IDA showing season.

As a group, we will learn through various means of presentation and then cook a meal that incorporates nutritional aspects to support the outcomes of the health condition. The goal is to learn, educate, cook, and eat. Nutrition is one of the most undervalued aspects of helping to treat and prevent chronic diseases since medicine and pharmaceuticals are usually chosen as the first option by physicians. Many patients are never introduced to the idea of making diet changes for the prevention and management of a disease and often suffer harmful side effects of drugs or are unresponsive to medicinal treatment. Through this club, we hope to show future healthcare workers the importance and value of good nutrition to make a bigger impact on patients.

clubs.description: Days for Girls at Penn State University is a student organization that promotes menstrual equity on campus, in the surrounding community, and worldwide. DfG PSU integrates sustainability and service within a welcoming and inclusive community. DfG takes a stand against period poverty (the lack of access to menstrual products and essentials needed for period care) by sewing reusable menstrual health kits, creating advocacy campaigns and educational workshops, and organizing fundraisers. The Days for Girls kit is a sustainable and cost-effective solution for menstruators experiencing period poverty. It lasts for five years and contains reusable liners, panty shields, and personal care products. When someone lacking access to menstrual products receives a Days for Girls kit, they also receive 3-5 years of comfort and dignity to continue attending school or work during their periods. In addition to sewing DfG kits, our Days for Girls club collaborates with other on-campus organizations to hold sewing events, leads campus discussions about global menstrual health issues, and advocates to end period poverty. clubs.name: Design for America at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Design for America (DFA) is a nationwide network of interdisciplinary student teams and community members using design to create local and social impact.
clubs.description: Design for America (DFA) is a nationwide network of interdisciplinary student teams and community members using design to create local and social impact. We teach human-centered design to young adults and collaborating community partners through extracurricular, university-based, student-led design studios tackling national challenges in the areas of education, health, economy and the environment. DFAers represent diverse academic fields such as engineering, design, technology, public policy, psychology, and economics. DFA believes that all students have the capacity to use design to innovate the world around them and DFA is a platform to do so.

clubs.name: Developers at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Developers at Penn State fosters a student developer community through hands-on projects, technical workshops, and industry connections. We partner exclusively with Google Developer Group to enhance professional development opportunities.

clubs.name: Diabetes Link at University Park
clubs.summary: Our Chapter of The Diabetes Link was founded for the purpose of connecting college students with and affected by Juvenile Diabetes in the hopes that these connections will create a support network.
clubs.description: Our Chapter of The Diabetes Link was founded for the purpose of connecting college students with and affected by Juvenile Diabetes in the hopes that these connections will create a support network which will enable students to fulfill their potential and limit the negative psychological and physical effects of Diabetes.

clubs.name: Digital Ethics Society at University Park
clubs.summary: The Digital Ethics Society is a student-led organization for those who are curious or concerned about the rapid evolution of technology and the consequences of its unregulated nature.
clubs.description: The Digital Ethics Society is a student-led organization for those who are curious or concerned about the rapid evolution of technology and the consequences of its unregulated nature.

clubs.name: Digital Media Group at University Park
clubs.summary: Digital Media Group is dedicated to professional development and community building among digital artists.
clubs.description: Digital Media Group is a collective of digital artists dedicated to community building and professional development. We're committed to helping those interested in a career in digital media find opportunities and make meaningful connections. Our members consist of illustrators, graphic designers, concept artists, 3D modelers, animators, and more! DMG is a place where digital artists work together to explore our rapidly expanding industries.

clubs.name: Digital Multimedia Design Club at World Campus
clubs.summary: DMD Club at Penn State World Campus aims to foster a student community for the DMD program and provide members with the opportunity to interact with professionals, alumni, and other students with similar interests and goal.
clubs.description: The Digital Multimedia Design (DMD) Club at Penn State World Campus aims to foster a student community for the DMD program and provide members with the opportunity to interact with professionals, alumni, and other students with similar interests and goals. In addition, the club strives to provide insight into current research practices and career options within the digital media and design fields.

clubs.name: Disability and Neurodivergence Affinity Group at World Campus
clubs.summary: We believe in the power of conversation and change to create an inclusive, open space for all students, neurodivergent, disabled and our allies through honest discussion, shared perspectives, and unwavering support.
clubs.description: At DNA (Disability and Neurodivergence Affinity Group), we are more than a support group, we are a community built on support, empowerment, and forward momentum. Open to all students. We believe in the power of conversation and change to create an inclusive, open space for all students, neurodivergent, disabled and our allies. Through honest discussion, shared perspectives, and unwavering support, we foster a platform where individuals can shape their own stories, challenge misconceptions, and advance our collective voice. At Penn State, "We Are" means something. It means no one stands alone, and there is always a Penn Stater by your side. It means we are shaped by our individual struggles but defined by our resilience and perseverance. We Are: made better by sharing our experiences, knowledge and building a community. We Are: The Disability and Neurodivergence Affinity. Supported by Penn State World Campus Student Affairs, DNA strives to celebrate strengths, advocate for visibility, and inspire real impact, not just within our university, but beyond. Here, we redefine what it means to belong, to be heard, and to thrive, ensuring that every student has the opportunity to push bound

clubs.name: Disability Law Caucus at Dickinson Law in UP
clubs.summary: Law School Org
clubs.description: Disability Law Caucus functions as both an affinity organizations for law students with disabilities and an interest group for law students focused on Disability Law.

clubs.name: Disc Golf Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To provide recreational and competitive opportunities in the sport of disc golf to Penn State students.
clubs.description: Welcome to Disc Golf Club! We are a super welcoming group to individuals of all skill levels! Our main objective lies in creating a community for those interested in Disc Golf :) Our weekly club rounds give students an opportunity to meet others interested in disc golf and switches around our local courses. These rounds promote an inclusive setting for anyone to come play, learn, and enjoy the sport. The competitive side of the club lies in College Disc Golf competitions where we travel and compete against other colleges. This side is geared towards more experienced players as there are limited spots available for each tournament. We've become a club sport at PSU, you can join us through PSU IMLeagues. If you are interested or have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out! As always, Happy Hucking!

clubs.name: Disciplemakers Christian Fellowship at University Park
clubs.summary: Christian Fellowship On Campus
clubs.description: DiscipleMakers is a local chapter of the Pennsylvania-based DiscipleMakers organization. Our purpose is to help people learn about Christianity, about why knowing Jesus matters, and about how to live out your faith day to day. We welcome everyone no matter what their background or interest level is. We seek to meet people where they are at and investigate who Jesus is and why he matters. We also place a high value on community and individual mentorship and investment. We do all of this through things like small group investigative Bible discussions, mentoring relationships, specific Bible study training, and through a loving and caring community. Since we are a local chapter of a larger organization there are also many opportunities to learn and grow through inter-collegiate conferences and service trips.

clubs.name: Discover
clubs.summary: This is Discover! Welcome to your Recognized Student Organization Management Platform! The summary section should include a slogan or tagline that represents your organization and it's goals.
clubs.description: Discover is Penn State's Recognized Student Organization (RSO) management and engagement platform. On Discover you can: -- Post Events & Track Attendance -- Recruit New Members -- Highlight Org Accomplishments to the entire university -- Manage your members through messaging listservs -- Create surveys, elections, and track service hours! If you have questions on how to get the most out of your OrgCentral page, email us at discover@psu.edu The Full Description section is a great opportunity to add an in-depth explanation of your organization and how it operates to achieve the goals that you have mentioned in your summary. Penn State Student Affairs: Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. Student Affairs is committed to building a community of belonging for all.

clubs.name: Disney Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Our mission is to provide members opportunities to share their passion for Disney, engage in Disney experiences, and connect with Disney professionals.
clubs.description: Disney Club at Penn State (DCAPS) is a student-run organization. Through weekly meetings, we participate in activities and discussions that foster our individual passions for all things Disney! We provide members the opportunity to find others with like interest and create an environment that fosters a strong community. We collaborate with Disney professionals to help members connect with individuals within the industry to build their network at Penn State and beyond.

clubs.name: Diversity in Healthcare Taskforce at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Diversity in Healthcare Taskforce at Penn State University Park, aims to educate undergraduate Pre-Health students about disparities in our healthcare system and empower them to become future healthcare providers who will tackle these issues.
clubs.description: The mission of the Diversity in Healthcare Taskforce is to foster meaningful dialogue and actionable solutions that reduce disparities in health communication and outcomes for historically marginalized communities. Through hosting an annual conference with keynote talks, interactive panels, and solution-focused sessions, the conference empowers the next generation of health professionals to recognize and address barriers rooted in culture, language, literacy, and access to technology. Then hosting a follow-up forum, the Solution Phase, where teams present practical interventions, tools, and projects inspired by conference discussions, with feedback from faculty, practitioners, and community leaders.

clubs.name: Dominican Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Welcoming environment for all students of Penn State to indulge and learn more about Dominican culture. This organization serves as a safe place for the Dominican members of the campus and a healthy learning and community experience for everyone
clubs.description: The Dominican Student Association was founded at the Pennsylvania State University on April 6th 2009. The Purpose of the Dominican Student Association is to increase campus understanding of the Dominican Republic as a nation, the Dominican-American experience, and the overall Dominican Culture. In addition this organization will serve as an avenue for students of Dominican heritage to unify, as well as medium for all those interested in exploring and celebrating Dominican culture. We strive to meet these goals through four different means, though we are not limited to these efforts: - Hosting and sponsoring informative and social events that will aid in addressing issues concerning Dominicans and other Latinos. These events shall be open to the entire Penn State community and the State College Community. - Also by concentrating our efforts on recruiting and retaining Dominicans students by developing academic and personal support networks for undergraduate students at Penn State. - Obtain historical and updated information about the Dominican Republic, in order to serve as a resource to Dominican affairs. - Strive to serve Dominican communities in the United States and abroad throu

clubs.name: Domino Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: We provide a space where anyone interested can come and play. We will teach you how to play strategically and enjoy the game of dominoes in collaboration with others.
clubs.description: The goal of this organization shall be to spread the culture, gameplay, and knowledge of the tabletop game of Dominoes and its many variations. Being that Dominoes is a game played worldwide, it has significance across many populations. Players will gain value from experiences when playing and will retain many principles pertaining to the game. We'll meet on a weekly basis and host events throughout the semester. Most important of all, we wish for everyone playing to have fun.

clubs.name: Don't Be Strangers at University Park
clubs.summary: Don't Be Strangers is a club working to bring students together.
clubs.description: Don't Be Strangers is a club working to decrease loneliness in an age of increased digital communication by bringing Penn State students together in person with games, movies, group trips, and various other activities. By getting off our devices and connecting in person we will no longer "be strangers" to each other and instead form strong, lasting friendships.

clubs.name: Downstagers at University Park
clubs.summary: The Downstagers is a small-scale theatre club with big ambitions. Our mission is to highlight the talents of our community and make a space for theatre to be accessible, inclusive and fun to everyone, no matter the level of experience.
clubs.description: The Downstagers is a small-scale theatre club with big ambitions. Our mission is to highlight the talents of our community through unique shows, put on in a fun, inclusive team environment. We welcome people with any range of experience. Whether you're on your tenth show or your first, you are welcome to participate in our productions. We highly encourage input from all members of the club throughout the creative process. If you are looking to take on a new position, from acting to tech, from crew to acting, from designing to directing, we are willing to work with you! Our club does events like musical read-throughs in a low-key, group setting for fun. We aim to put on one show per semester, usually with smaller-cast musicals, or student-written shows. If you have an idea for a performance, we want to hear it!

clubs.name: Ducks Unlimited at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Ducks University chapters are playing an increasingly important role in Ducks Unlimited's conservation mission. DU recognizes that a vibrant and strong collegiate program is the key to a healthy future for wetlands conservation.
clubs.description: The Ducks University chapter program began in 1984 at the University of Texas at Austin and the Tiger Chapter, Baton Rouge, LA. Since then, the number of active chapters in the United States has steadily increased. In 2023, 105 active chapters were responsible for raising $2.9 million dollars in event income for wetland conservation. An annual highlight of the Ducks University chapter program is "Third Term," a collegiate leadership summit held in August where college volunteers from across the country come to Ducks Unlimited National Headquarters to learn about conservation, leadership skills, and fundraising techniques. Today, Ducks University chapters are playing an increasingly important role in Ducks Unlimited's conservation mission. DU recognizes that a vibrant and strong collegiate program is the key to a healthy future for wetlands conservation, and a strong emphasis will continue to be placed on the development of what has been a very successful program. Ducks University volunteers get involved for a variety of reasons including: • Social functions that build community • School pride • DU merchandise • Conservation education • Resume building &bull

clubs.name: Dungeons & Dragons and More at World Campus
clubs.summary: We Are: building a community around tabletop gaming at Penn State World Campus! We're open to everyone, regardless of experience level, setting or the rule set you prefer. It's a place to connect with others in an informal setting, and play some games!
clubs.description: We Are: building a community around tabletop gaming at Penn State World Campus! We Are: open to everyone, regardless of experience level, setting or the rule set you prefer. It's a place to connect with others in an informal setting, and play some games! Join us for ongoing campaigns, one-shots, learn to play or GM sessions and much more. We meet as a whole club every other month but have events and ongoing games throughout the semesters!

clubs.name: Dungeons and Dragons at University Park
clubs.summary: Dungeons and Dragons Club is a club designed to organize and facilitate the creation of D&D (Dungeons and Dragons) groups at Penn State University and to host D&D related events.
clubs.description: Welcome, adventurers and to those prospecting to be one! We are Dungeons and Dragons Club, a club for those who enjoy tabletop role-playing games. Though we are primarily a Dungeons and Dragons Club, we welcome other types tabletop role playing systems, so bring your favorites! If you have never played Dungeons and Dragons or other games, no worries! We accept and encourage all experience levels. Our club affords players and Dungeon Masters the ability to open and join campaigns with greater ease by providing a large group of eager players and Dungeon Masters searching for campaigns and players. Our meetings give time for Dungeon Masters to pitch their campaigns, and our Discord gives players a chance to communicate with Dungeon Masters and view a spreadsheet of open campaigns. The link to this chat is found below, and is where you will find most of the information and announcements: Penn State D&D Club Discord Our club meets weekly on Fridays at 6:00 in 160 Willard Building*. We hope to see you there! *Location may change in the near future

clubs.name: Eagles Autism Foundation College Program at University Park
clubs.summary: The Eagles Autism Foundation raises funds for autism research and care programs, promotes inclusion across all Eagles events, and aims to inspire and engage the community so we can provide much-needed support to make a lasting impact in the autism field.
clubs.description: Championed by Eagles Chairman and CEO Jeffrey Lurie, EAF aims to inspire and engage the community, so that together, we can provide much-needed support to make a lasting impact in the field of autism. 100% of the EAF proceeds go back into research and the community. The EAF College Program is designed to educate students, faculty, and staff about autism and neurodiversity while raising funds for groundbreaking research and care programs. Through advocacy, empathy, and unity, we are making a transformational impact in the autism community, bringing awareness to action. The goals of the EAF College Program are to inspire and engage the campus community, support EAF's mission by hosting fundraisers on campus, educate students, and provide volunteer opportunities for hands-on experience with the autism community.

clubs.name: Early Career Professionals Group
clubs.summary: The Student Affairs Early Career Professionals Group aims to provide opportunities to grow socially, professionally, and educationally through engaging meetings and conversations with peers who are in their first seven years of Student Affairs work.

clubs.name: Earth and Mineral Sciences Living Learning Community at University Park
clubs.summary: The Earth and Mineral Sciences LLC (Living Learning Community) exists to provide a live-in community that promotes a favorable academic and social atmosphere for students pursuing degrees within the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences.
clubs.description: Welcome to Irvin Hall, the Living Learning Community for students within the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences! As the LLC of the College of EMS, Irvin Hall seeks to promote academic involvement within the college by providing resident and non-resident members with ample opportunities to network with faculty and staff within the college, connect with students who have similar interests, and participate in community-building events hosted throughout the academic year!

clubs.name: Earth and Mineral Sciences Student Council at University Park
clubs.summary: Provides a vital link between students, administration, and community in an attempt to enrich the intellectual and social atmosphere of the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences.
clubs.description: The college of EMS Student Council provides a vital link between students, administration, and community in an attempt to enrich the intellectual and social atmosphere of the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. Our meetings are held on alternating Wednesday evenings at 6pm with our THON Organization with some combined Student Council/THON meetings. Throughout the semester we host many events to help enrich the atmosphere of the college. We host professional development events such as faculty-student dinners, breakfast with the deans, and events with the Graduates of EMS (GEMS). We also host many social events such as a homecoming celebration in the fall, the college's semi-formal night (Gala) in January, an end of the year picnic in May, as well as many other smaller events throughout the year. All students, including those outside of the College of EMS, are welcome to join!

clubs.name: Earth House at University Park

clubs.name: Earthquake Engineering Research Institute at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: EERI PSU Student Chapter fosters the understanding of earthquake resilience in communities by sharing fundamental knowledge and learning from professional practice and research experiences. The student organization is comprised of student body members.

clubs.name: East African Student Association at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: To educate, promote, and celebrate the East African (EA) diaspora and aim to convey the culture and customs of the EA nations.
clubs.description: The East African Student Association (EASA) is dedicated to celebrating and sharing the rich cultural heritage of East Africa, connecting students from Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Djibouti, Tanzania, Somalia, Rwanda, Burundi, Sudan, South Sudan, and Eritrea. Through cultural events, discussions, and educational programs, we foster unity, appreciation, and understanding of East African traditions. EASA also provides professional development, networking, and mentoring opportunities to empower its members academically and beyond. Committed to inclusivity, we encourage students from all backgrounds to engage in cross-cultural dialogue, celebrate diversity, and contribute to a vibrant and united East African presence on campus. We organize events to showcase East African and broader African cultures through music, art, food, and traditions, creating an immersive and educational experience for the entire campus community.

clubs.name: East Asia Dialogue Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The East Asia Dialogue Club (EADC) fosters dialogue among students from China, Korea, Taiwan, and other East Asian regions, as well as peers from diverse backgrounds, to promote cultural understanding, debate, and mutual respect.
clubs.description: The East Asia Dialogue Club (EADC) is dedicated to fostering dialogue and understanding among students from mainland China, Taiwan, and other East Asian regions, as well as students from diverse cultural backgrounds at Penn State. The organization provides a neutral and open platform for cultural exchange, discussion, and debate on topics ranging from shared traditions to contemporary social and political issues. By encouraging respectful dialogue and critical reflection, EADC aims to reduce stereotypes, deepen mutual understanding, and build bridges across cultures.

clubs.name: East Halls Residence Association at University Park
clubs.summary: As EHRA, we aim to provide a platform for students to collaborate, create, and lead change within East Halls.
clubs.description: East Halls Residence Association is committed to ensuring a democratic, safe, fun, and well-organized living environment in the East Housing Area through the student government presence, otherwise known as the East Housing Residence Association (EHRA). EHRA is composed of an executive cabinet and representatives of leaders from within the residential area. Our student-run organization works under The Association of Residence Hall Students (ARHS) and is a pillar of Residence Life + the Nittany Chapter of the National Residence Hall Honorary (NRHH). EHRA serves as the official voice for the East residential student population, providing advocacy, leadership, fun activities for the community, and encourages civic engagement. The EHRA believes that happiness begins in the home and is committed to providing a safe and happy environment for all residents across Martin, Tener, Geary, McKean, Pinchot, and all other residents' halls in the area. Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. Student Affairs is committed to building a community of belonging for all.

clubs.name: Eberly College of Science Achieving Change of Campus Excellence in Student Success at University Park

clubs.description: The mission of Eclipse is to raise money primarily for patients of pediatric cancer, with an important secondary interest in the treatment of victims of malaria and community service. In addition, we are very interested in establishing an organization that promotes teamwork, social impact, and developing the leaders of tomorrow through community and global activism. -- Eclipse was founded in 2016, and its short tenure at Penn State, has become the largest THON Org on campus. In Eclipse, we care about building family and creating long lasting relationships. -- Please check out our Instagram @EclipsePSU or our website eclipsepsu.org for more information about joining Eclipse!

clubs.name: EcoAction at University Park

clubs.description: The Economics Association (est. 1968) is an organization of students with a passion for economics, who wish to grow both academically and professionally outside of the classroom. We enrich the educational experience of our members with academic presentations, written publications, economic simulations, and various other activities. We prepare our members for post-graduation by offering career fair preparation, improving résumés, and connecting them with companies.The Association offers leadership opportunities and experience in planning events and communicating in a team. Overall, we provide our members with an environment where they can meet people who share their interests, make new friends, and succeed at Penn State and beyond.

clubs.name: Education and Public Policy Undergraduate Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Connect with peers, build professional skills, and prepare for careers in education policy through networking, workshops, and mentorship.
clubs.description: This organization is specifically designed for undergraduate students majoring in Education and Public Policy, Integration and Undergraduate (IUG) students, and Education Policy Studies minors at Penn State. Our goal is to foster a supportive community where students can connect with peers who share a passion for education policy. Through networking, workshops, and collaborative projects, members will have the opportunity to: - Build professional skills that prepare them for careers in higher education, law, government, research, think tanks, K–12 education policy, and related fields. - Learn from guest speakers and alumni who are currently working in education policy and public service. - Engage in discussions about current issues that are shaping schools and education systems. - Receive guidance on navigating the IUG pathway, internships, and career opportunities. Our mission is to strengthen connections, provide meaningful professional development, and prepare students to become leaders and advocates in the field of education policy.

Residents connect through social events, workshops, and shared experiences that build friendships and prepare them to make an impact in schools and communities.

clubs.name: Education Leadership Student Association at University Park

clubs.description: The mission of this organization is to foster a vibrant and inclusive community for all graduate students in Educational Leadership, empowering them to build meaningful professional networks, exchange innovative research ideas and findings, and cultivate lasting social connections through collaborative events, workshops, and informal gatherings. By promoting these opportunities, we aim to enhance academic growth, career advancement, and a sense of belonging within the field.

The intention of the association is to provide a forum for support, discussion, scholarship, social networking, and professional development relating to all matters of PK-20 education.

clubs.summary: Active membership of the Education, Development, and Community Engagement Graduate Student Association (EDCE GSA) consists of registered graduate students in the Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education's EDCE Program.

clubs.summary: The Educational Equity Scholars Living Learning Community (LLC) welcomes incoming first-year students who are committed to engage with peers from various backgrounds, perspectives, and identities.
clubs.description: The Educational Equity Scholars Living Learning Community (LLC) welcomes first-year students who are committed to engaging with peers from various backgrounds, perspectives, and identities. Through experiential learning programs that help students transition to college and build a strong academic foundation, we aim to foster a sense of belonging, purpose, and joy for all our residents. In addition to the LiveOn experience, LLC members are encouraged to enroll in the Educational Equity Scholarship and Community Seminar in the fall and spring semesters and engage with their mentors in the Office of Scholars Programs (OSP) and the various colleges. The LLC houses all first-year scholarship recipients through OSP, which includes Bunton-Waller Fellows & Merits, Lenfest Scholars, Maguire Scholars, Milton Hershey Scholars, and Commonwealth Scholars as well as students who elect to join this vibrant community which engages in frequent team building activities, social events, and relevant programs to meet students' needs. The LLC features live-in undergraduate Program Assistants who are former residents of the LLC and serve as a mentors and resources to scholars during this important transi

clubs.name: Egyptian Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of the Egyptian Student Association is to familiarize Penn State students with the rich Egyptian culture & history, as well as integrate the Egyptian students with the Penn State Community.

clubs.name: EHouse at University Park
clubs.summary: Provides students with a constructive and positive live-in community that creates and supports projects, activities, and social events relevant to students with majors in the College of Engineering.
clubs.description: Penn State Engineering House (E-House) hopes to provide students with a constructive and positive live-in community that supports projects and activities relevant to their majors within the College of Engineering. E-house is conveniently located in McKee Hall, a sector of the West Halls residence area sited next to Recreation Hall and the Lion Shrine. E-House is considered a co-ed special living option, available only to those full-time students accepted into the College of Engineering at University Park. E-House provides students with the opportunity to take on leadership roles through various executive positions and committees within the house. In addition, E-house supports numerous social events, such as sporting events and picnics, to promote a sense of community and friendship among its members. In order to continually improve the living environment, members of E-House have the opportunity to attend house meetings where they may offer opinions and suggestions. Overall, E-House's commitment to its members offers a comfortable living environment where engineers may share their common interests through their studies and their social involvement.

clubs.name: Electronic Dance Music Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To provide a welcoming atmosphere for electronic dance music enthusiasts by establishing social events to share music, while simultaneously promoting local and Penn State student DJ's and music producers.
clubs.description: EDMC is an inclusive atmosphere fostering a nonjudgmental welcoming EDM community. We have monthly non-mandatory meetings to discuss new music, plan events, and other club activities. The club's main events are an annual showcase in the hub, supporting local DJs at venues downtown, and occasionally traveling together to concerts. We also provide DJ workshops for those interested in DJing.

clubs.name: Emergency Management at Penn State World Campus
clubs.summary: The purpose of the organization is to guide aspiring emergency managers to finding a career in the field of emergency management and achieving their Certified Emergency Manager (CEM) designation.

clubs.description: Empowering Women in Law (EWIL) is a progressive and inclusive organization dedicated to fostering gender equality within the legal field. Through its multifaceted initiatives, EWIL aims to provide a supportive platform for undergraduate students interested in pursuing careers in law, regardless of gender identity. At the core of EWIL's mission is the empowerment of women in the legal profession, recognizing the historical and systemic barriers they have faced. Founded at Michigan State University in 2018, EWIL has grown into a national, gender-inclusive organization dedicated to supporting students interested in law-focused careers. Established in spring 2021, our Penn State chapter connects students with shared interests, fostering a supportive space to discuss and navigate the unique challenges and opportunities for women in law. At EWIL, we value camaraderie, achievement, and empowerment, striving to uplift women and girls in both educational and professional settings. Together, we provide guidance and encouragement for law school applications, LSAT preparation, and the pursuit of successful careers in law.

clubs.description: Who are we? Engineers in Action is a service organization that strives to bring together students of all backgrounds to revitalize communities by constructing pedestrian footbridges over impassable rivers. During the rainy seasons, many communities do not have safe means to cross flooding rivers separating them from their markets, healthcare, and education. Isolation caused by impassable rivers is a root cause of poverty all over the world which is why EIA's mission is to empower today's students to become tomorrow's global leaders by building bridges with under-served communities. What do we do? EIA's Bridge Program envisions a world in which global citizens connect across cultures to improve quality of life and ensure geography doesn't determine access to opportunity. This is why we have participated in 7 international bridge-building trips that take place for multiple weeks during the summer. Penn State EIA has had the opportunity to build bridges in Panama, Rwanda, and Bolivia. Every year, we select a team of about 4 to 8 students to participate in these life-changing projects. clubs.name: Ethics in Science and Medicine at University Park
clubs.summary: Ethics in Science and Medicine will encourage informed discussion of topics relating to bioethics.
clubs.description: The purpose of this club is to bring awareness to and discuss the plethora of bioethical issues faced by our society. These are not limited to dilemmas faced by people in the science community, but are, rather, issues that encompass a broad range of scenarios that occur in everyday life. The goal of this organization would be to facilitate informed discussion by inviting guest speakers from within the Penn State community and from government or industry to discuss their experiences with bioethics in their respective roles. Topics covered would include, but would not be limited to, ethical theories and frameworks, animal testing, clinical trials, differences between academia and industry, climate science, health insurance, and the controversies and politics surrounding these topics. Current events involving bioethics, in particular, will be emphasized.

The org will include a team of students to compete in the College Fed Challenge. The organization is designed to create a competitive team with the ultimate goal of winning the College Fed Challenge. During the competitive season, the team will analyze current market data to create a 15 minute presentation which will be submitted to the Federal Reserve Board. clubs.summary: The mission of the University Park Fee Board is to augment the out-of-classroom experience for all undergraduate and graduate students at University Park. We accomplish this through the responsible and equitable stewardship of the Student Initiated Fee.
clubs.description: The University Park Fee Board Each year, students pay one comprehensive fee referred to as the "Student Initiated Fee." In the 2016-2017 academic year, the inaugural University Park Fee Board was formed. The Board heard over a dozen allocation requests from various administrative entities as well as requests from the University Park Allocation Committee (UPAC), which allocates funds to student organizations. Currently, the Board funds over 23 units across the University. The UP Fee Board is comprised of 13 voting members. The presidents of both the University Park Undergraduate Association (UPUA) and the Graduate and Professional Student Association (GPSA) are members of the Board, and each appoints additional members. The UPUA President appoints three members, while the GPSA President appoints two. The final members of the board are six At-Large members who are selected through an application and interview process held each spring semester. The diverse composition of the Board allows for collaboration and deliberation on allocation decisions. Members participate in group practices, ice shows, and club events while enjoying the opportunity to skate with teammates who share their passion. The competitive team is a larger commitment and represents Penn State at intercollegiate competitions within the Southeast Section. Each season, the team travels to three sectional competitions with the goal of qualifying for the U.S. Intercollegiate Figure Skating Championships (Nationals). Penn State Club Figure Skating is a highly ranked program, consistently placing among the top 16 teams in the nation out of more than 220 collegiate programs. clubs.description: The Glee Club is an auditioned ensemble of 50-65 tenor/bass voices singing music from medieval chant to commissioned twenty-first-century choral works. Rehearsal and performance of music composed for lower voices from the sixteenth to the twentieth centuries, including sacred and secular compositions. The Glee Club performs on campus at least once per semester, tours yearly, and has performed throughout Pennsylvania, the United States, Europe, and New Zealand. The goal of the ensemble is to provide artistic, meaningful, and successful choral performances. To achieve this goal, the learning objectives for individual students include attention toward individual vocal development, increased musicianship skill, and the discovery of new means of artistic expression. In addition to these individual objectives, the conductor of the ensemble also teaches directly toward the objectives of ensemble tone, blend, balance, intonation, dynamics, diction, phrasing, etc. Grades are determined by a combination of vocal and musicianship assessments (both written and aural) and attendance at rehearsals and performances. The ensemble is directed by Dr. Christopher Kiver, Director of Choral Activities.
