clubs.summary: The GLOBE is a Living Learning Community for students in the Schreyer Honors College. It seeks to form a close-knit community of globally minded individuals who have the desire to foster global awareness and an international perspective.
clubs.description: The GLOBE aims to expand on the initiatives of the Schreyer Honors College by: Fostering respect and awareness for the world and its diverse people Contributing to international progress by developing a network for future collaborations Building an inclusive community that embraces different mindsets and encourages personal and academic growth To attain this goal, members participate in activities such as group discussions, guest professor events, and food events. In order to ensure that all members on the floor are active, a point system is in place on the floor. Members accrue points by attending floor events and must accrue 10 points by the end of each semester to remain part of The GLOBE.

clubs.name: Gluten Avoidant Society at University Park
clubs.summary: The Gluten Avoidant Society gives students, who are gluten free, celiac, or gluten-free curious, a community to meet others and learn about PSU resources. This club hosts gluten friendly events, restaurant visits, baking days, and more!

clubs.name: Gongfu Cha Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To promote and preserve the art of Traditional Chinese Tea Ceremony (Gongfu Cha) through scholarship, research, and outreach.
clubs.description: We specialize in a cultural artform surrounding the Chinese language, history, aesthetics, agriculture, preservation, and recovery of lost knowledge through the traditional practice of Gongfu Cha.

clubs.name: Google Developer Groups on Campus at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: GDG@PSU is a student-led tech community that explores Google technologies through workshops, projects, and hackathons. We connect students with industry resources, foster hands-on learning, and build an inclusive developer ecosystem at Penn State.
clubs.description: GDG on Campus – Penn State University (GDG@PSU) is the official student chapter of Google Developer Groups On Campus. Our mission is to create a collaborative and inclusive environment for students passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving. We host hands-on workshops, coding competitions, speaker sessions, and collaborative projects covering Google technologies such as Android, Flutter, Firebase, TensorFlow, and Google Cloud. Beyond technical skills, GDG@PSU emphasizes professional development, networking, and open-source contributions. Our community is open to students from all majors and experience levels—whether you’re a beginner curious about coding or an advanced developer seeking to expand your expertise. By joining GDG@PSU, you’ll gain access to exclusive resources, mentorship opportunities, and a network of peers driven to build, learn, and grow together.

clubs.name: Goth Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: PSU Goth Club is an organization dedicated to engaging with and sharing goth culture. The club focuses on music and aesthetics and is open to all who are willing to learn and create a welcoming environment.
clubs.description: Goth Club at Penn State is Penn State's premier goth music and subculture organization! WHO WE ARE: Founded in Sept. 2023 out of a small study room in Davey Laboratory, our goals are to provide a safe space for alternative and goth individuals, as well as all marginalized groups. We share a unified love for all things goth, from music to fashion to literature and beyond! WHAT WE DO: Presentations educating about Goth subculture and music, goth group dinners (encouraging being visibly goth/alt in Penn State + State College), tabling, relaying community resources, music nights, movie nights, game meetings, general hangouts, collabs with other RSOs, and more!

clubs.name: Graduate Alliance for the Liberal Arts at University Park
clubs.summary: The Graduate Alliance for the Liberal Arts (GALA) is a graduate student organization at Penn State University dedicated to building interdisciplinary community and connection across the liberal arts.
clubs.description: The mission of the Graduate Alliance for the Liberal Arts (GALA) is to foster interdisciplinary community, advocacy, professional development, and scholarly collaboration among graduate students within the liberal arts at Penn State University. GALA seeks to create an inclusive and supportive environment that promotes intellectual engagement, creative exchange, graduate student well-being, and opportunities for social and professional connection across departments and disciplines.

clubs.name: Graduate and Professional Outdoor Club at University Park
clubs.summary: GPOC is a community of graduate and professional students interested in learning about and engaging with outdoor activities. Whether you’re a pro or have no experience, everyone is welcome to join, there’s always more to learn and people to meet!
clubs.description: The Graduate and Professional Outdoor Club is an inclusive community of graduate and professional students with a shared interest in engaging in outdoor activities. GPOC strives to lower any barrier to participation in outdoor activities by making technical and safety skills available, facilitating carpooling as well as the use of gear and equipment, and connecting members with on and off-campus outdoor resources and providing a space for stewardship of the outdoors. To keep up with events and chat with members, fill out this form to join our WhatsApp group: https://forms.gle/nqAHixa7yBTePHfT9

clubs.name: Graduate and Professional Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of the Graduate and Professional Student Association (GPSA) is striving to enrich the experience of graduate and professional students.
clubs.description: The mission of the Graduate and Professional Student Association (GPSA), in striving to enrich the experience of graduate and professional students, shall be to provide: a unified and informed voice representing graduate and professional students to the University's administration, Board of Trustees, academic units, and other external organizations that make decisions on behalf of students; a forum to address the ideas and concerns of graduate and professional students; support of scholarly activities and professional development; leadership, social, and service opportunities to the graduate and professional student body; and, events and activities to promote a sense of community among graduate and professional students and their families.

clubs.name: Graduate Art Education Association at University Park
clubs.summary: To create community engagement, professional and academic development, and leadership through the arts and arts education.
clubs.description: WHAT IS GAEdA? GAEdA is a Penn State graduate student organization that creates community engagement, professional and academic development, and leadership through the arts and arts education. OUR MISSION The mission of GAEdA is to represent and support the interests of graduate students in art education. GAEdA exists to enrich the experiences of graduate students through social and professional networks. MENTORSHIP GAEdA is committed to creating an inclusive and supportive environment for our members. GAEdA mentorship program provides new graduate students in their first year with graduate student mentors who are in their third semester or greater. This program encourages both mentors and mentees to learn from one another, grow as individuals, and expand both professional and social networks in a supportive environment.

clubs.name: Graduate Research and Innovative Design at University Park
clubs.summary: The purposes of the Penn State Graduate Research and Innovative Design (GRID)Organization are:A. To provide design research support for students from the College of Arts and Architecture.B. To increase visibility of ...
clubs.description: The purposes of the Penn State Graduate Research and Innovative Design (GRID)Organization are: A. To provide design research support for students from the College of Arts and Architecture. B. To increase visibility of new knowledge production and advancements in design disciplines. C. To encourage collaborative research development.

clubs.name: Graduate Special Education Research Collaborative at University Park
clubs.summary: The Graduate Special Education Research Collaborative is dedicated to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment for graduate students interested in research development for individuals with disabilities.
clubs.description: The Graduate Special Education Research Collaborative is dedicated to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment for graduate students interested in research development for individuals with disabilities. Our mission is to provide mentorship to new graduate students, empower fellow students, and champion the rights and opportunities of individuals with disabilities. We strive to cultivate meaningful dialogue on critical issues in special education, promote diversity and equity within our community, and encourage collaboration that advances research and practice. Through these efforts, we aim to build a connected, informed, and compassionate community committed to creating positive change for all.

clubs.name: Graduate Student Affinity Group at World Campus
clubs.summary: This affinity group is designed to bring graduate students together for connection, collaboration, and mutual support. It aims provide members a space to share resources, tips, and strategies for academic and personal success while building community.
clubs.description: This is a welcoming community designed to bring graduate students together for connection, collaboration, and mutual support. This group provides a space to share resources, tips, and strategies for academic and personal success while building meaningful networks across disciplines. Whether you're looking for advice, accountability, or simply a community that "gets it," this group is here to help you thrive in graduate school and beyond. Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. Student Affairs is committed to building a community of belonging for all.

clubs.name: Graduate Student Association for Visual Culture at University Park
clubs.summary: Welcoming students from all disciplines, GSAVC fosters interactions between graduate students with the aims to open challenging dialogues and to consider how complementary fields can inform scholarship and practice in visual culture.
clubs.description: Welcoming students from all disciplines and backgrounds, the Graduate Student Association for Visual Culture (GSAVC) is a multi-disciplinary group whose aims are to foster the interaction between graduate students beyond their fields, to open challenging and new dialogues, and to consider how complementary disciplines can inform scholarship and practice in visual culture.

clubs.name: Graduate Student Association in Information Sciences and Technology at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of GIST can be summarized as the following: 1.Provide the graduate students of IST with information deemed necessary by the University or the College; 2.Discover and share practical resources for graduate students
clubs.description: The mission of GIST can be summarized as the following: 1.Provide the graduate students of IST with information deemed necessary by the University or the College; 2.Discover and share practical resources for graduate students—for individual and collegial success; 3.And facilitate social, as well as intellectual, peer-to-peer communications, connections, and support.

clubs.name: Graduate Students in Communication at University Park
clubs.summary: To plan graduate events, assist with administration in the College of Communications with incoming student orientation, and offer various academic and social opportunities to students in the College of Communications.
clubs.description: The Graduate Students in Communications (GSIC) is an organization of graduate students within the Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications. We organize academic and social events that foster professional growth, collaboration, and community building. Additionally, GSIC serves as a liaison between graduate students, faculty, and staff within Bellisario College. Our efforts include supporting student orientation, assisting with administrative tasks, and providing resources for conference preparation and funding opportunities.

clubs.name: Graduate Students in the Department of Geography at University Park
clubs.summary: To advance the graduate program in the Department of Geography through supporting scholarly activities and professional development, and by providing leadership, service, and scholarship opportunities.
clubs.description: The purpose of GS-DOG is to advance the graduate program in the Department of Geography through supporting scholarly activities and professional development, and by providing leadership, service, and scholarship opportunities.

clubs.name: Graduate Women in Engineering at University Park
clubs.summary: GradWIE welcomes people of all gender identities to support the personal and professional wellbeing of engineering graduate students through peer support, the creation of safe spaces, social events, diverse resources, and professional development.
clubs.description: GradWIE aims to create an inclusive community to support the success of engineering graduate students. We explore and highlight the engineering experience through a lens focused on gender, but we do not exclude other foci or experiences. GradWIE welcomes people of all gender identities to support the personal and professional wellbeing of graduate students through peer support, the creation of safe spaces, social events, diverse resources, and professional development.

clubs.name: Graduate Women in Science at University Park
clubs.summary: Furthers women's interests in science, serves as a support and networking group for women in science, and provides a society for women's recognition as scientists.
clubs.description: The Penn State chapter of Graduate Women in Science is a dynamic and inclusive community dedicated to advancing women and underrepresented groups in science. We go beyond professional networking—our mission is to build meaningful connections across disciplines, foster lifelong friendships, and create a supportive environment for all members. We provide a safe space where individuals can express themselves, share their experiences, and receive the support they need to thrive in their academic and professional journeys. While our primary focus is on supporting women and female-identifying graduate students, we welcome all who are committed to our mission of fighting inequality and promoting diversity in STEM. We believe that true progress is made through collective action, and our community stands united in the belief that the pursuit of equality is a shared responsibility, one that is best achieved together.

clubs.name: Graduates in International Languages and Literatures at University Park
clubs.summary: Create a network of support for new and continuing graduate students in the department of Comparative Literature.
clubs.description: We create a network of support and community for graduate students in the department of Comparative Literature, and host events promoting critical study of international literatures for the benefit of all Penn State graduate students in the Liberal Arts.

clubs.name: Graduates in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of the GWGSS is to represent and support the interests of graduate student majors and minors in Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, as well as those who are interested in or affiliated with the program. ...
clubs.description: The mission of the GWGSS is to represent and support the interests of graduate student majors and minors in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, as well as those who are interested in or affiliated with the program. The GWGSS exists to enrich the experience of said graduate students through creating intellectual networks and providing leadership, social, and professional opportunities, as well as to ensure adequate and fair representation of graduate student interests within the Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies program. The GWGSS accomplishes these goals through various events intended to promote intellectual community both within the graduate student community and between graduate students and faculty.

clubs.name: Groove Dance Association at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Groove Dance Association brings fun, fitness, and community through Hip-Hop and Street Jazz classes. No performances, just good vibes and growth — plus fundraising events to keep the groove going!
clubs.description: Groove Dance Association is an all-inclusive, non-performing dance club that creates a welcoming, energetic space for all skill levels. We specialize in Hip-Hop and Street Jazz, offering weekly masterclasses that are fun, lighthearted, and focused on growth and community. Our classes are more than dance — they're a workout for your body and mind! Like a fitness class, each session builds strength, stamina, flexibility, and mental wellness, all while connecting with others in a supportive, judgment-free environment. Beyond classes, Groove Dance Association is proud to fundraise for THON, supporting the fight against childhood cancer. We host events and collaborations throughout the year to raise funds and awareness, while also creating fun, meaningful ways for our members to get involved. Whether you're a seasoned dancer or just starting out, Groove Dance Association is the perfect place to move, connect, and thrive. Come dance with us, stay active, make new friends, and be part of a community that celebrates YOU

clubs.name: Growth International Volunteer Excursion at Penn State University Park

clubs.summary: The Gujarati Student Association is a cultural organization aiming to spread Gujarati culture and unite people through food, festivities, and fun.

clubs.name: Habitat For Humanity at University Park
clubs.summary: The Habitat for Humanity Campus chapter partners with the local Habitat for Humanity chapter to volunteer on builds, repairs and at the local Restore. We are dedicated to serving the community and helping provide affordable housing for those in need.
clubs.description: Habitat for Humanity Campus chapter at Penn State is a student-led organization dedicated to serving the local community through hands-on construction and service. In partnership with the Greater Centre County Habitat for Humanity, members volunteer on new home builds, repairs, and restoration projects to help provide safe and affordable housing for families in need. Beyond the build site, the club also supports the community by participating in local events and advocating for affordable housing.

clubs.name: Hack at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: To organize and run a bi-annual collegiate hackathon at Penn State, and promote social programming by hosting workshops, talks and other tech-centric events.
clubs.description: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iI4AXgKzBQU HackPSU is Penn State's largest student-run collegiate hackathon. Over 500 students join us nationwide each semester for a weekend of creation, innovation, and fun. All are welcome, from seasoned coding veterans to first-time hackers from any major or field. Join the HackPSU Team today! HackPSU's member recruiting season is at the beginning of each semester. Please visit us at the involvement fair or email us at team@hackpsu.org!

clubs.name: Happy Valley Christian Community at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of Happy Valley Christian Community is to follow Jesus and befriend people from all countries of the world.
clubs.description: The purpose of Happy Valley Christian Community is to follow Jesus and befriend people from all countries of the world. We believe that love is the most powerful force in the world and that we should extend this love even to those who dislike us or hate us. We believe that a deep love for God and others is the best possible foundation for building intentional communities, strong families, and vibrant churches. We frequently host discussion forums on these and many other topics. We also host cultural events, Bible studies, Christian Worldview classes, seminars, and more. We seek to promote the teachings and values of Jesus and his Apostles and we endeavor to live them out in a manner similar to the early Christians. HVCC facilitates connections between the student community and the local community and partners with LifeQuest community. Bible studies are held at the address below! 105 Pickwick Ave State College, PA 16803

clubs.name: HEAL: Help Every Angel Live at University Park
clubs.summary: HEAL is a group of Penn State students devoted to finding a cure for pediatric cancer and helping every angel live. Our focus is to financially and emotionally support the families and children affected; the family we espe...
clubs.description: HEAL is a group of Penn State students devoted to finding a cure for pediatric cancer and helping every angel live. Our focus is to financially and emotionally support the families and children affected; the families we especially sponsor are the Tuckey and Hess Families. We raise money for the Four Diamonds Fund through THON, a 46-hour dance marathon. We put a focus on joining as a group to benefit THON.

clubs.name: Health and Human Development Office for Career Development at University Park
clubs.summary: Dedicated to enriching human well-being and strengthening intellectual, social, physical, economic, and emotional wellness, Penn State’s College of Health and Human Development (HHD) will give you a solid foundation for positively impacting people!
clubs.description: Welcome to the HHD Office for Career Development! We are committed to helping you turn your passion into a fulfilling career. Whether you're exploring career paths, preparing for internships, or planning for graduate school, our team is here to support you every step of the way. We offer career coaching, professional resources, and opportunities to connect with employers and industry leaders in fields like public health, nutrition, kinesiology, human services, healthcare business, and more. No matter where you are on your career journey, we're here to help you gain the skills, confidence, and connections you need to succeed. Start with a career assessment Understanding your interests, values, personality, and skills is key to finding possible career paths, building a community on campus around shared interests, and gaining valuable experiences that set you up for success beyond campus. The Focus2 assessment gets to the core of what drives you and provides suggestions for career paths to explore. After you complete the Focus2 assessment, schedule an appointment with our office to discuss your results and longitudinal professional development. Career Exploration Resources ✨Focus2- in

clubs.name: Health and Physical Education and Coaching Club at University Park
clubs.summary: We are a group of aspiring HPE teachers and Coaches who are excited to learn from each other, grow as future professionals, and have fun!
clubs.description: Our organization is looking to help future Health and PE teachers and Coaches meet each other early on in their PSU journey. Members will also have the opportunity to attend the state-wide SHAPE PA conference to connect and learn from professionals in the field. Other events we plan to hold throughout the year will include sports tournaments, jump rope for heart with local schools, as well as many other activities.

Through student fairs and other resources, we work to grow our club and welcome those interested in joining a big Greek family. The organization enjoys discussing and learning about Greek culture, holidays, landscapes, etc. to better enhance our inclusivity at Penn State. Through launching and coordinating events to build an intercultural community, we hope to see you at our next event and are happy to answer any questions.

clubs.name: Helping Hands in Healthcare at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Helping Hands in Health is an undergraduate organization that is committed to providing a space for pre-med or pre-PA students to gain valuable mentorship experience (either as a mentor or mentee) in their pre-health journey at Penn State.
clubs.description: GENERAL BODY MEETINGS biweekly! Schedule for the FA26 semester: Helping Hands in Health is an undergraduate organization that is committed to providing a space for pre-med or pre-PA students to come with questions and gain insight into core components of medical (and physician assistant) school. The main component of our organization is to provide mentorship to freshman and sophomore pre-med/pre-PA undergraduates and allow junior or senior pre-med/pre-PA undergraduates to gain valuable leadership experience as mentors. This creates a judgment-free space for freshmen and sophomores to come with questions, ask study questions, learn more about required examinations for acceptance to PA or medical school, and more!

clubs.name: Helping Hearts at University Park
clubs.summary: Helping Hearts is a support system for survivors of domestic violence as they rebuild their lives. We work to help those we can, educate the community, challenge misconceptions, and promote a deeper understanding of domestic violence.
clubs.description: Helping Hearts is committed to supporting survivors of domestic violence while also raising awareness about the issue. By offering resources, mentorship, and advocacy, we can help individuals regain independence and rebuild their lives. In addition to providing emotional and practical support, we work towards educating the community, challenging misconceptions, and promoting a deeper understanding of the complexities of domestic violence. Through awareness we can try and prevent future abuse and empower survivors on their journey to healing.

clubs.name: Hershey Kisses at University Park
clubs.summary: Our mission is to help families fight pediatric cancer by coming together and raising money for THON and the Four Diamonds Fund. We are paired with 4 awesome families and support them along their cancer journeys through fundraisers and gatherings.

clubs.name: HHD Engaged Learning at Penn State
clubs.summary: Explore opportunities for engagement with engaged learning activities and experiences through the College of Health and Human Development.
clubs.description: Engaged learning refers to the out-of-class experiences that enrich the college experience through hands-on activities and reflection. This includes opportuniuties such as global engagement and education abroad, research and fellowships, student organizations, service and civic engagement, career and professional development, and leadership development. In the College of Health and Human Development, engaged learning opportunities are intentionally created to meet the unique needs of our students.

clubs.name: Higher Education Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The Higher Education Student Association (HESA) promotes student engagement through community building and peer-to-peer support in professional and scholarly endeavors for Penn State’s residential and World Campus higher education communities.

clubs.name: Hillel at University Park
clubs.summary: Penn State Hillel’s mission is to enrich the lives of the 6,000 Jewish students at Penn State so that they may enrich the Jewish people and the world. PSH's students and staff are dedicated to creating a pluralistic, welcoming, and inclusive environment.
clubs.description: Penn State Hillel's mission is to enrich the lives of the 5,000 Jewish students at Penn State so that they may enrich the Jewish people and the world. Penn State Hillel's student leaders, staff, and lay leaders are dedicated to creating a pluralistic, welcoming, and inclusive environment for Jewish college students, where they are encouraged to grow intellectually, spiritually, and socially. Penn State Hillel helps students find a balance between being distinctively Jewish and universally human by encouraging them to pursue tzedek (social justice), tikkun olam (repairing the world), and Jewish learning, and to support Israel and global Jewish peoplehood. Penn State Hillel is committed to excellence, innovation, accountability, and results.

clubs.summary: Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA) is a blend of historical recreation, martial art, and combat sport, mostly focused on studying sword-based manuscripts from the 15th to 18th centuries.
clubs.description: Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA) is a blend of historical recreation, martial art, and combat sport, mostly focused on studying sword-based manuscripts from the 15th to 18th centuries. Currently only permitted padded boffers as per University safety regulations.

clubs.summary: Provides a forum for interaction among professors and students concerning the study of history.
clubs.description: The history round table club is a place for all Penn State student that are interested in learning more about or discussing our favorite events and periods in history. Every topic is open to discussion as well as a democratic system for members to vote on activities such as watching movies and historical excursions. Guest lecturers will also be invited to talk about certain time periods or events the group is interested in.

clubs.summary: We strive to empower a diverse generation of leaders and scholars who promote human health, development and quality of life throughout the lifespan through various perspectives, education and discussion of social determinants of health.

clubs.name: Homecoming at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of Penn State Homecoming is to celebrate tradition and instill pride in all members of the Penn State family through active engagement of students, alumni, faculty, & staff across the community.
clubs.description: Penn State Homecoming is one of the largest student-run homecoming organizations in the country, which aims to celebrate tradition and instill pride in all members of the Penn State family through active engagement of students, alumni, faculty and staff across the community. Our organization is comprised of many student volunteers who donate their time to creating a multitude of events that make the Homecoming celebration a yearlong event. Students work with their peers, alumni, corporate sponsors, and various other community members to help make Homecoming Week and our other annual events occur. Homecoming maintains lasting relationships with those in and outside of Penn State University to ensure a successful celebration each year.

clubs.name: Homecoming Committee at World Campus
clubs.summary: The Homecoming Committee will work with University Park for future homecoming celebrations. The committee’s main tasks will include activity planning and coordination for the event.
clubs.description: The homecoming committee is a fun and exciting team that plans events, selects court members, builds excitement, and works with other organizations to pull off an amazing week of celebrating the spirit of Penn State. To pull this off, we have general meetings monthly on the Last Thursday of Every Month and continue to work throughout the months on Teams. We have a few teams within that you can work specifically, in if it is something that meets your interest. Our teams are led by our executive team members and include Media & Marketing, Alumni Relations, Court Relations, Technology, Merchandising, and Events.

clubs.name: Honor Guard at University Park
clubs.summary: Supports and represents Penn State University and the 720th Cadet Training Wing Honor Guard. Provides color guards and ceremonies to the State College community and performs at competitions and events with rifle trick and drill teams.
clubs.description: Honor Guard is a professional organization committed to the service of others through military ceremony and community outreach. As an organization, we support not only the Penn State AFROTC Detachment, but other organizations including the VFW, Penn State Athletics, Scouts, JROTC and more. We have the opportunity to honor those who have honored us through ceremonies like the POWMIA table, Color Guards, and Saber Arch. This organization also competes in Military Excellence Competitions including rifle drill and exhibition drill.

clubs.name: Horn Society at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Penn State Horn Society's mission is to provide its members a venue for performance opportunities, educational trips, hands-on skill building classes, and access to master classes and lectures regarding the instrument.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Penn State French Horn Ensemble is to provide members of the horn studio a venue for performance opportunities, educational trips, hands-on skill building classes, and access to master classes and lectures regarding the instrument. It is comprised of music majors and talented hornists from outside the School of Music by audition. The group performs regularly at various on-campus events, and has been invited to perform at the Symposium of the International Horn Society on numerous occasions., The Penn State French Horn Ensemble has also performed at Mid-West Regional Horn Workshops as well as the Eastern Division Music Educators National Conference. The ensemble exposes students to a vast collection of repertoires encompassing original works and arrangements of romantic, baroque, classical, impressionist, and popular music.

clubs.name: Horticulture Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Establishes and develops a spirit of unity, friendship, and sociability among the students and faculty members of the College of Agricultural Sciences and beyond, and stimulates greater student interest in horticulture, landscaping, and sustainability.
clubs.description: Horticulture Club is an organization for all University Park students interested in plants, gardening, and landscaping. It is the goal of the club to educate both its members and the public on the Green Industry as a whole, sound horticultural practices, and new techniques. The largest event that the club conducts throughout the year is its annual Horticulture Show. For this event, the Snider Agricultural Arena on campus is transformed into a full-fledged indoor landscape in which all of the plant material is sold to help fund the club. Other events throughout the year include attending and competing in the annual National Collegiate Landscape Competition, organizing flower sales and plant sales, going on field trips, hearing from guest speakers in the industry, and participating in community service. Meetings are every other Wednesday at 6:00 in Tyson Headhouse I, Classroom 123. Follow the club on Instagram and Facebook for their meeting schedule and to stay up to date!

clubs.name: HOSA-Future Health Professionals at University Park
clubs.summary: HOSA provides a unique program of leadership development, skill development, community service, and recognition for secondary, postsecondary and collegiate students enrolled in Health Science Education Programs.
clubs.description: HOSA-Future Health Professionals is an international student organization endorsed by the U.S. Department of Education and the Health Science Education (HSE) Division of ACTE. Our two-fold mission is to promote career opportunities in the health care industry and to enhance the delivery of quality health care to all people. HOSA's goal is to encourage all health occupations instructors and students to join and be actively involved in the HSE-HOSA Partnership. As a chartered state association member of HOSA, the Pennsylvania program provides a unique program of leadership development, motivation, and recognition exclusively for middle school, secondary, postsecondary, adult, and collegiate students enrolled in HSE programs. HOSA's mission is especially critical when considering the acute shortage of qualified workers for the health care industry.

clubs.name: Hospitality Financial and Technology Professionals at Penn State University Park

clubs.description: The Hospitality Financial and Technology Professionals allows students to explore the financial and technological side of the hospitality industry. Students have the opportunity to delve into topics that interest them and aid in future endeavors. Students are given insight on the career paths that are available in the hospitality industry.

The chapter creates opportunities for students to engage directly with industry professionals through networking events, guest speakers, workshops, and conferences such as the HSMAI Intercollegiate Conference. In addition to professional development, the organization emphasizes leadership, collaboration, and real-world experience, allowing members to build meaningful connections and gain practical insights that support their transition into the hospitality industry.

clubs.name: Hotel and Restaurant Society at University Park
clubs.summary: Impacts hotel, restaurant and institutional management students by connecting them with industry professionals and alumni with real networking opportunities.
clubs.description: PSHRS is the umbrella student organization in the School of Hospitality Management, and also serves as the student chapter of the School of Hospitality Management's 9,000-member-strong alumni society. All students upon their entry into the program become members and may continue as a member of the alumni chapter of this group upon graduation. The purpose of the organization is to unite and build closer fellowship among the students, alumni, and faculty of the school with the objectives of strengthening all the professions of the program and building the reputation of the school. Student members can be active in any of the committees of the club: education, alumni relations, social, fundraising, and community service. This organization provides trips to Washington, D.C. and the Annual HX: Hotel Experience in New York City.

clubs.name: HUB-Robeson Center
clubs.summary: The HUB-Robeson Center is the student union for Penn State University, University Park.
clubs.description: As a center of University community life, the HUB-Robeson Center complements the academic experience by offering students opportunities in leadership, social responsibility, citizenship, volunteerism, and student employment. The HUB-Robeson Center provides a variety of cultural, educational, social and recreational programs through boards, committees, student organizations, and staff. The HUB-Robeson Center encourages self-directed activities providing opportunities for individuals to recognize their own competencies, learn the dynamics of group activity, and understand their role as responsible citizens. The HUB-Robeson Center strives to provide an environment, which fosters respect, values all individuals, appreciates diversity and celebrates the contributions of all its members. Penn State Student Affairs: Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. Student Affairs is committed to building a community of belonging for all.

clubs.name: HUB-Robeson Galleries
clubs.summary: Bringing diverse and contemporary art exhibitions to the entire University community. The HUB-Robeson Galleries are Free For All, Always.
clubs.description: Welcome to HUB-Robeson Galleries! HUB-Robeson Galleries program two physical gallery spaces HUB Gallery and Art Alley, five display cases, murals, and public projects across the University. Bringing diverse and contemporary art exhibitions to the entire University community, the HUB-Robeson Galleries are Free For All, Always. Find Current Exhibitions on our website If you are interested in collaborating or scheduling a tour (virtual or in-person) with your student org, contact Sarah Kipp smk201@psu.edu Vision HUB-Robeson Galleries value the transformative power of art and artists. Led-by and for students, we activate the arts in order to address today's complex questions and serve local and global communities. Working to advance diversity, equity, expression, and access in all their forms, we prioritize inclusions as an essential element and core strength of our public service mission. Free for all, we work to expand access to the arts through cross-disciplinary and discovery-based processes. clubs.name: Human Capital Advisory Group at University Park
clubs.summary: The Human Capital Advisory Group connects Penn State students with opportunities to explore human capital management and organizational development through workshops, networking, and professional growth programs.
clubs.description: The Human Capital Advisory Group at Penn State is a student-led organization dedicated to exploring careers, concepts, and best practices in human capital management, organizational development, and people-focused consulting. Our mission is to prepare students for impactful careers by providing professional development workshops, guest speaker events, networking opportunities, and collaborative projects. We aim to create a supportive space where members can develop leadership skills, understand workforce trends, and connect with professionals in consulting, human resources, and related fields. By bridging academic learning with real-world applications, we help members build the knowledge and experience needed to excel in people-driven business roles

clubs.name: Immigration Law Society at Dickinson Law in UP
clubs.summary: The Immigration Law Society’s aim is to expose students to current issues in Immigration Law, educate its members on the different facets of immigration law in practice, and to encourage an empathetic approach to immigration law.
clubs.description: The goal of the Immigration Law Society is to bring together students who are interested in the growing practice of Immigration Law. The Society is premised on education and networking in the field of immigration law, exposing students to the various areas of immigration law (such as Family-Based Immigration, Asylum Law, Removal Proceedings, and Business Immigration Law), and demonstrate how Immigration Law has the potential to intersect with other fields of law (such as criminal law, labor law, family law and constitutional law). The Society hosts meetings that showcase guest speakers from the field, pro-bono clinics in collaboration with local and national humanitarian clinics, and interactive events with various types of practitioners (such as immigration lawyers, judges, attorneys from U.S. Department of Homeland Security, officers from U.S. Customers and Border Protection, defense attorneys, and representatives of public interest and charitable organizations).

We are dedicated to promoting the academic success of indigenous students on campus through the advancement of indigenous awareness, recruitment, retention, and social activities! IPSA aspires to meet the needs of the greater Indigenous community by supporting on-campus initiatives related to issues in the American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, Indigenous Pacific Islander, etc., communities. Each season the team will create a new routine and perform at local TIA competitions in hopes to grow and improve the show as the season continues. As a club sport at Penn State University, it provides opportunity for students to develop teamwork, leadership, and artistic skills while engaging in consistent practice and performance schedules. The group focuses on creativity, athleticism, and discipline, bringing together people of all different backgrounds with dance and performance. The Indoor Winter Guard aims to foster a supportive, welcoming environment where members can push themselves, grow as performers, and contribute to the vibrant culture of Penn State's arts community. The Indoor Winter Guard strives for excellence in competition and promotes school spirit for the teammates and their supporters. ITE Pennsylvania State University (Penn State ITE) is a volunteer-run student community who are interested in exploring or aspiring to be future transportation professionals. We are affiliated with the ITE Mid-Atlantic Section and ITE Mid-Colonial District. We provide opportunities for learning and networking, including connection to the local, regional, national, and international community of transportation professionals.

Whether you're looking for information or simply a friendly face, ITSA is here for you. At Penn State, we're more than just classmates—we're family. clubs.description: The Penn State Investment Association (PSIA) exists to teach its members about investing and the finance industry. PSIA is open to students of all ages and all majors at University Park. To be a part of the organization, students need to attend the general body meetings on Wednesday nights and sector breakout meetings on Sunday afternoons. No prior investing or finance knowledge is required to join. In PSIA, students can expect to learn basic and advanced investing concepts, the current state of the stock market and economy, valuation methodologies and how to apply them, and how to best position yourself to pursue a career in the finance industry and on Wall Street. Members also have the opportunity to participate in a mock portfolio challenge, stock pitch competition, and networking events. PSIA also serves as the feeder organization to the Nittany Lion Fund, which is Penn State's ~$20 million student-run hedge fund. At the end of each semester, PSIA analysts can apply and interview for a spot on the Nittany Lion Fund. In order to be eligible, PSIA analysts must be a freshman or sophomore.

Whether you're interested in event planning, marketing, fundraising, or simply supporting a meaningful cause, Lend A

clubs.description: Letters of Love Global is an organization started by a young girl from Minnesota named Grace Berbig. Grace says, "Lots of people ask what inspired me to start Letters of Love. My answer, in short, is my mom. When I was ten my mom lost her battle to cancer. I have been on a mission to create a kinder world and support patients ever since. She is, and forever will be, to thank for every accomplishment Letters of Love has made and will continue making." (quote from www.lettersoflove.com) Letters of Love has grown tremendously over the years, now represented in 17 countries with 270+ clubs and donating over 250,000 cards to children in hospitals. Penn State's passion for fighting the battle against childhood cancer makes it the perfect space for a club like this. There are far too many children suffering from terminal illnesses and we are here to make sure they know they aren't doing it alone. We want them to know they have the support of the entire Penn State student body. For more information about Letters of Love at Penn State find us on Instagram @lettersoflovepsu To learn more about the organization as a whole go to @lettersofloveglobal on Instagram or visit their website www.lett

clubs.description: Letters to Beverly was created to connect generations through a simple pen pal program. Students within this organization will have the opportunity to connect with a resident of a retirement home by writing letters back and forth throughout the year. Our organization strives to emphasize the importance of connecting generations and bringing joy to the lives of others. Note from the creator of Letters to Beverly: "My name is Natalie Isett. When I was young, my great grandmother, Beverly, and I started writing letters to each other. These letters meant so much to the both of us. I wanted others in her generation to have a connection with someone just like I did with her. In high school, I started a pen pal program with a local retirement home and named the program after my great grandmother. In this program, students were paired with a retirement home resident, and they wrote to each other throughout the year. This program brought so much joy to both the students and residents. I am so happy to have the opportunity to bring this program to Penn State and to continue to spread that joy."

The Liberal Arts Ambassadors work directly with the College of the Liberal Arts' Office of Undergraduate Admissions, assisting the recruitment team with developing and staffing programming for prospective and admitted students. They additionally organize a number of professional development workshops, academic panels, community opportunities, and social events each semester for organization members. clubs.summary: Lift the Mask Club aims to reduce the stigma of mental health illnesses. It also aims to increase awareness and to seek solutions to many problems related to mental health in our country through meetings/other events that talk openly about mental health.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Lift the Mask Club is to reduce the stigma of mental health illnesses. It also aims to increase awareness and to seek solutions to the many problems related to mental health in our country. We have biweekly meetings and provide opportunities for club members to openly discuss issues, stories, and other aspects related to mental health. We will provide resources (hotlines, websites, organizations) to the members of our club that relate to that topic of the meeting. We also plan to have events across campus such as yoga, dog petting, and other events that will reduce stress and promote positive mental health. The club is sponsored by the Quell Foundation, who was created by PSU alumnus, Kevin Lynch. The Quell Foundation provides scholarships for students affected by a mental health illness and aims for these students to advocate and spread more awareness about mental health in their collegiate communities. We will encourage our club members to advocate and apply for scholarships for the Quell Foundation as well. Feel free to join our GroupMe: https://groupme.com/join_group/88633968/cWy0RceL

clubs.description: Lions for the U.S.- Israel Alliance is a student organization dedicated to educating, engaging, and empowering students through opportunities in advocacy, public policy, leadership development, and civic engagement. The organization seeks to strengthen understanding of the U.S.-Israel relationship and the democratic process through educational programming, discussions, guest speakers, and hands-on experiences. Members will have opportunities to participate in advocacy initiatives, lobbying efforts, leadership training, filmmaking and media projects, policy discussions, and networking opportunities with professionals in government, public affairs, and nonprofit leadership. Lions for the U.S.- Israel Alliance aims to develop informed student leaders who are passionate about civic participation, constructive dialogue, and building strong relationships between the United States and Israel. The organization welcomes students of all backgrounds who are interested in learning more about public policy, international affairs, leadership, and advocacy while gaining practical skills that can be applied both on campus and in future professional careers.

clubs.description: Lutheran Student Community is a relaxed community where students find a welcoming approach and support for their journey of faith. Whether you've grown up in a church or are new to faith you are welcome. Worship and other activities are grounded in the priorities and values of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (ELCA), but you don't have to be Lutheran to feel at home. Gatherings are casual and inclusive. Weekly worship is designed to be relevant to student lives. Weekly dinner is informal and provides free food. Lutheran Student Community will welcome you into this community of faith where people talk, listen & share the challenges and joys of campus life, explore who God is, and help you find for yourself what place God has in your life. Come as you are. Really. Check our socials and website for more information (including our calendar) Mission Statement: As believers in Jesus Christ, the Penn State Lutheran Community is committed to: Welcoming all the name of Jesus, Embracing Personal Growth and understanding, Exploring the connections between God's Word and the world, Preparing to follow Jesus' example with our lives, So we may go forth in a celebration of God's Love.

clubs.description: Penn State Lyrical Line Dance Company, primarily known as PLL Dance Co., is the university's premier lyrical dance company. While our name highlights lyrical style dance, we are open to and embrace other genres like contemporary, jazz, and even occasionally hip hop! We consist of about 30-40 girls and rehearse throughout the school year to prepare for our biannual showcases. Our rehearsal schedule is designed to be flexible with each members' schedule so our dancers are not limited in what they can participate in at school! We have a 2-hour mandatory full company rehearsal every Sunday and members can sign up for additional 30-minute small group classes throughout the week that will all be performed at showcase. We also participate in many fun events like homecoming, THON, bonding activities throughout the year. While dance is a huge passion of ours, at the end of the day, PLL is a family first. Many of us are close friends, roommates, and even sisters. You will never feel alone at Penn State when you are part of the PLL Family!

clubs.name: MEDLIFE Chapter at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: MEDLIFE Chapter at Penn State, University Park raises money for Medicine, Education, and Community Development projects for low-income families around the world. Members can participate in a MEDLIFE Service Learning Trip that travels to communities!
clubs.description: The Penn State University Park chapter of MEDLIFE (Medicine, Education, and Development for Low-Income Families Everywhere) is a student-led organization committed to combating poverty through global and local service. Established in August 2023 by Biobehavioral Health student Emily Monigle, the chapter has rapidly grown, engaging over 150 members in its first year . MEDLIFE at Penn State aligns with the broader MEDLIFE Movement, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that partners with underserved communities in Latin America and Africa to improve access to healthcare, education, and community development . The chapter's initiatives include:​ Service Learning Trips (SLTs): In May 2024, approximately 20 members participated in an SLT to Lima, Peru, collaborating with local medical professionals to provide healthcare services to underserved communities .​ Fundraising Efforts: The chapter successfully raised $2,365 to support MEDLIFE's mission, contributing to projects such as building safe housing, constructing essential infrastructure, providing critical medical care, and advancing educational opportunities

clubs.summary: Provides aspiring players a chance to play regardless of talent; active participation is dependent on the desire to play and willingness to pay for one's own expenses.
clubs.description: The club hockey team competes at the Div. 2 level in the American Collegiate Hockey Association. They are a highly competitive team that practices several times a week and travels around the country during their season. The club hockey team is for experienced hockey players who have played travel and/or high school hockey prior to attending Penn State and have open tryouts every year.

clubs.name: Men's Lacrosse Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Provides Penn State students the opportunity to play organized lacrosse as an alternative to the existing varsity lacrosse program.

clubs.name: Men's Water Polo Club at University Park
clubs.summary: As a team, we promote the sport of water polo, and represents Pennsylvania State University in the Collegiate Water Polo Association on the club level. We work to be our best selves in and out of the pool, in our community, and as a team.
clubs.description: Please feel free to get to know more about all aspects of our team through our website. If you have any questions, please contact us at pennstatemenswaterpolo@gmail.com. This team is always looking for new players interested in learning and competing in our sport. We are excited to meet you! Penn State Men's Club Water Polo (pennstateclubwaterpolo.com)

clubs.name: Mending Walls at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Mending Walls at Penn State is a club inspired by the mural project Mending Walls, created by Hamilton Glass in Richmond, Virginia. We organize an annual community mural at Penn State and host social events throughout the year!
clubs.description: A Penn State organization affiliated with Mending Walls RVA, where we strive to build a diverse community and start conversations about topics that shape who we are as individuals and as a whole.

clubs.name: Meteorology and Atmospheric Science Graduate Student Organization at University Park
clubs.summary: MASGO is a student-run organization that advocates for graduate students in the Department of Meteorology and Atmospheric Science.
clubs.description: MASGO serves as the oversight committee for all affairs that affect graduate students in the Department of Meteorology and Atmospheric Science. MASGO shall advocate for and represent all graduate students within the department. MASGO shall also serve as a liaison between the graduate students and the department, college, and university.

clubs.name: Mexican-American Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Promotes unity between students of different races; encourages and motivates individuals to further their education; obtains political, social, and cultural awareness.
clubs.description: The Mexican-American Student Association was founded by Gonzalo Cano in 2004 as a way to represent and highlight Mexican culture here at Penn State. MASA is not only for Mexican-American students but for anyone who is interested in learning more about Mexican culture and meeting new members! Our meetings consist of workshops, information sessions, game nights, and volunteering events!

clubs.name: Middle Eastern & South Asian Law Students Association at Dickinson Law in Carlisle
clubs.summary: Middle Eastern and South Asian Law Students Association at Dickinson Law (Carlisle)
clubs.description: MESALSA (Middle Eastern and South Asian Law Students Association) is a student organization at many law schools that supports students with ties to the Middle East and South Asia. It focuses on building community, promoting cultural awareness, and providing academic and professional support. MESALSA often hosts networking events, panels, and social gatherings, and advocates for issues affecting its members within the law school and broader legal community.

clubs.name: Middle Eastern and North African Caucus at University Park
clubs.summary: MENA Caucus is for all Undergraduate/Graduate students who identify with Arab culture or have a desire to learn more about it! We seek to create a hospitable environment where we discuss sociopolitical issues, mingle, and broaden our networks.
clubs.description: Biweekly GBMs, social events, volunteering and community service. Visit our instagram (@psumenacaucus) to stay up-to-date!

clubs.name: Middle Eastern and Northern African Business Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Empowering MENA leaders at Penn State Business Networking Growth Join us for events, opportunities & connections!
clubs.description: The MENA Business Association at Penn State connects students with the business landscape of the Middle East and North Africa. We bridge Penn State and the MENA region through education, networking, and professional development. Through speaker events, industry discussions, and hands-on learning, we provide insights into international business, finance, trade, and entrepreneurship. By partnering with professionals and global organizations, we create opportunities for career growth and cross-cultural understanding.

clubs.name: Military Law Caucus at Dickinson Law in Carlisle
clubs.summary: Military Law Caucus at Dickinson Law (Carlisle)
clubs.description: MLC is focused on the study and discussion of legal issues related to the armed forces. It provides opportunities for students to learn about topics such as military justice, national security law, and veterans' legal issues through events, speakers, and networking. The caucus also supports students interested in careers with the military, government, or related legal fields.

clubs.name: Military Law Caucus at Dickinson Law in UP
clubs.summary: MLC

clubs.name: Military Service Organization at World Campus
clubs.summary: The Military Service Organization at Penn State World Campus is a recognized Student Veterans of America chapter.
clubs.description: The Military Service Organization at Penn State World Campus is a recognized Student Veterans of America chapter. The Military Service Organization’s efforts are focused on the mutual aid, social and intellectual growth, and preservation of the common interests of students in our communities who are veterans, active duty, military spouses, and allies of the Armed Forces.

clubs.name: Millennium Society
clubs.summary: The purpose of the Millennium Society is to promote diversity in STEM and provide service to the community through the Millennium Scholars Program, including but not limited to science outreach at Penn State and participation in THON.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Millennium Society is to provide service to the Millennium Scholars Program and the K-12 education system. This includes but is not limited to social events, science outreach, and community outreach.

clubs.name: Mindfulness and the Science of Happiness Club at University Park
clubs.summary: MASH holds weekly meetings (Wed @ 6:15 PM in Rackley 209) where students come together to explore mindfulness-based and scientifically validated topics related to well-being, stress-reduction, and human happiness to support our own pursuits of happiness.
clubs.description: The college experience is one that includes joys and moments of profound realizations, but it also includes challenges and the pressure to accomplish more, to balance between work and social life, and to discover for oneself what it means to be happy. The goal of MASH is to create a non-judgmental space where students can come together to explore mindfulness-based and scientifically validated practices related to stress reduction, well-being, and human flourishing to help support our own pursuits of happiness. We will delve into researched topics that center around what it means to live a life of happiness, purpose, social connection, and resilience.

clubs.name: Mini-Golf Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The Mini-Golf Club at Pennsylvania State University was created to inspire fun and laughter through the means of mini-golf amongst undergraduate students.
clubs.description: The Mini-Golf Club at University Park is dedicated to creating a fun and safe environment for undergraduate students to connect and play mini-golf. Weather permitting, we organize outdoor minigolf events in the Fall and Spring semesters.

clubs.name: Mining Society at University Park
clubs.summary: Promotes learning opportunities and assists with professional development in the mining industry to students in mining engineering, civil engineering, environmental engineering, industrial engineering, and other related majors.
clubs.description: Penn State Mining Society is the student chapter of the Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration (SME). Our main goal is for students to expand their knowledge, create networks and and obtain internships and full-time positions within the mining and heavy civil industry. We do this by providing our members with out of the classroom learning opportunities, conference trips, and weekly informational meetings.

clubs.name: Minorities in EMS at University Park
clubs.summary: Minorities in EMS (MEMS) will empower the diverse community within the College of Earth Mineral Sciences, foster a sense of community, and promote professional development within the members prospective fields of study.

clubs.name: Minorities In Sports Next: Penn State Chapter at University Park
clubs.summary: Official Penn State affiliate of the Minorities in Sports professional network
clubs.description: Minorities in Sports Next: Penn State Chapter strives to unite students with a passion for sports, inform them on industry career options, and provide other resources beneficial to their success. We aim to provide students with access to the national MIS network dedicated to breaking down barriers for minorities to pursue a career in the sports industry. In doing these things, we intend to increase diversity on the business side of sports in order to better reflect the minority athletes who play the game.

clubs.name: Minority Association of Pre-Medical/Health Students at University Park
clubs.summary: As a chapter affiliated to the Student National Medical Association, the purpose of the Penn State Minority Association of Pre-Medical/Health Students (M.A.P.S.) is to increase the number of minority students entering/completing health professions.
clubs.description: The Minority Association of Pre-Medical/Health Students is a national organization affiliated to the Student National Medical Association. As a national organization that has numerous chapters across America, the purpose is to increase the number of underrepresented students entering and completing health professional education. Through efforts from the national, regional, and Penn State chapter we hope to follow the steps to Aid in the implementation of workforce diversity Reduce and eliminate health disparities through education Increase the number of minorities entering health professional schools Support people of color as they proceed in their pre-medical/health journey here at Penn State

clubs.name: Minority Women In Health Fields at University Park
clubs.summary: Our mission is to empower minority women in health fields through mentorship, networking, and professional development. We will provide resources, raise awareness on industry challenges, advocate for diversity, and engage in community outreach for impact
clubs.description: Minority Women in Health Fields is a club dedicated to supporting and uplifting minority women pursuing careers in health-related fields. Through mentorship, professional development, and educational initiatives, we provide resources to navigate challenges in the healthcare industry. Our organization fosters career growth through networking events, guest speakers, and skill-building workshops on resume writing, interview preparation, and leadership. Additionally, we advocate for diversity in healthcare by engaging in community outreach, volunteer work, and discussions on workforce disparities. Together, we strive to create a more inclusive and equitable future in healthcare.

clubs.name: Mock Trial Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The Mock Trial Association is dedicated to educating its members on the fundamentals of trial advocacy, providing abundant opportunities for student leadership, and competing at the regional and national levels of the American Mock Trial Association.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Penn State Mock Trial Association is to encourage and promote an appreciation of the skills necessary to successfully practice trial advocacy through courtroom workshops, intramural competitions, and intercollegiate competitions. The association also sponsors and manages the Penn State AMTA team(s), which represents the University at the regional and national levels of Mock Trial Competition. The organization is designed to be a competitive organization with the ultimate goal of winning the American Mock Trial Association National Championship Tournament each year.

clubs.name: Model Aircraft Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Model Aircraft Club at Penn State is a local student chapter of the Academy of Model Aeronautics. We help students enjoy the hobby of RC flying at Penn State by providing safe and legal avenues to learn how to fly unmanned aircraft and drones.
clubs.description: The Model Aircraft Club at Penn State is a University Model Aviation Student Club (UMASC) chartered with the Academy of Model Aeronautics (AMA). As such, we can offer our members discounted AMA membership. Our goal is to help students enjoy the hobby of RC flying and model aviation in general. Our members have varied interests including fixed-wing RC aircraft, quadcopters, and drones.

clubs.name: Model Railroad at University Park
clubs.summary: The Model Railroad Club strives to educate members and the public on the value of railroads through building and operating model railroads with all involved fields, including woodworking, electrical work, art design, history, and more.
clubs.description: The Penn State Model Railroad Club, founded in 1955, is centered around building and operating model railroads in different scales. We invite everyone, experienced or not, to join us and learn about the history of railroads and the roles they play in society, along with benchwork, electrical engineering, landscaping, diorama building, and much more. The hobby of model railroading revolves around so much more than trains; this niche hobby truly has something for everyone.

clubs.name: Molecular, Cellular, and Integrative Biosciences Graduate Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of the Molecular, Cellular, Integrative Biosciences Graduate Student Association (MCIBS GSA) is to unite the students of the MCIBS graduate program via building an inclusive professional, social and intellectual community.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Molecular, Cellular, Integrative Biosciences Graduate Student Association (MCIBS GSA) is to unite the students of the MCIBS graduate program by building an inclusive social and intellectual community through recreational and professional events. The MCIBS GSA will also serve as a liason between the department chairs, faculty and graduate students. The organization will invite speakers of interest and aid new students in acclimating to State College.

clubs.name: More Than Medicine at University Park
clubs.summary: This club's mission is to educate our community regarding various medical concepts and concerns to ultimately promote and contribute to a healthier and stronger society.
clubs.description: This club's mission is to educate our community regarding various medical concepts and concerns to ultimately promote and contribute to a healthier and stronger society. We aim to provide our members with information regarding volunteer opportunities, research opportunities, and more to strengthen their medical school applications.

clubs.name: Mortar Board at University Park
clubs.summary: Mortar Board is a national junior and senior honor society. We provide opportunities for personal, academic, and professional development to our members, and host events that not only benefit Penn State students, but the greater community as well!
clubs.description: Mortar Board is a national junior and senior honor society. We provide opportunities for personal, academic, and professional development to our members, and host events that benefit Penn State students and the greater community.

clubs.name: Movin' On at University Park
clubs.summary: To organize and manage an annual spring music festival, to promote the talent of student bands, to collaborate with other student organizations and keep the interests of the student body in mind, and to do so in a substance free environment.
clubs.description: Penn State's Annual Student-Run Music Festival
