clubs.summary: Moving Party at Dickinson Law (Carlisle)

clubs.name: Mu Sigma Upsilon Sorority, Inc. at University Park
clubs.summary: In 1981, our founding mothers saw the need for a sorority that crossed the societal boundaries of race, religion, culture, and class. While other Greek organizations are and continue to grow more diverse, our organization foundation is based on diversi...
clubs.description: In 1981, our founding mothers saw the need for a sorority that crossed the societal boundaries of race, religion, culture, and class. While other Greek organizations are and continue to grow more diverse, our organization foundation is based on diversity and our sisters embrace multicultural ideals and interests; we speak to use our sorority as a vehicle to educate the surrounding campus and community on issues of diversity. We recognize that diversity is not limited to race, and we are proud to say we have achieved a sisterhood which is quite diverse with respect to not only race, but religious heritage, geographic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, nationality, political ideology, and even choice of major and career. Ultimately, multiculturalism is the belief that there is inherent value in discovering, understanding, and appreciating all the ways in which people are different from each other. It is for this reason that we differentiate ourselves, in name and in purpose, from Greek organizations with the word "MUlticultural".

clubs.name: Multicultural Education Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: To develop a supportive coalition of underrepresented students of color within the College of Education, aimed at promoting feelings of inclusion within the college community.
clubs.description: Are you looking to find a home in the College of Education? By joining our student organization you will have the chance to make positive connections with your peers, create strong connections to multicultural alumni, and receive peer mentoring support. MESA is open to both undergraduate and graduate students in the College of Education! No matter who you are or where you come from, we welcome everyone. Our mission is to create an inclusive community for underrepresented students in the College of Education. We aim to provide them with a sense of community through engagement of a variety of activities which promotes a feeling of empowerment. We also want to help our fellow members and peers establish their identity throughout their college career. Finally, we aim to equip students with a firm network which will provide them with the necessary tools to succeed. Stop by Chambers 123 and say hello to us in The Office of Education and Social Equity! We would love to have you in our diverse community.

clubs.name: Multicultural Engineering Graduate Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The Multicultural Engineering Graduate Association is a graduate student organization that commits itself to support multicultural graduate students in the STEM fields.
clubs.description: The Multicultural Engineering Graduate Association (MEGA) is a student organization that fosters equity, inclusion, recruitment of, and belonging for graduate students in engineering and science disciplines across the Penn State, University Park campus. Through social events, workshops, and its alumni network, MEGA serves graduate students' needs for a collegial community of their peers and professional development. As an organization, we strive to create a welcoming community and support for our members that will bolster their overall Penn State experience.

clubs.name: Multicultural Greek Council at University Park
clubs.summary: The Multicultural Greek Council at Penn State University was established in the Fall of 2001. The MGC represents the numerous culturally and religiously diverse social fraternities and sororities at The Pennsylvania State University.
clubs.description: The Multicultural Greek Council at Penn State University was established in the Fall of 2001. The MGC represents the numerous culturally and religiously diverse social fraternities and sororities at The Pennsylvania State University and acts as the supervising governing body for them. Currently, MGC governs 7 different fraternities and sororities. MGC strives to support its members by providing a safe space that allows the free exchange of ideas, programs, and services between our fraternities and sororities. Our goal is to promote academic excellence and multiculturalism through advocacy, philanthropy, cultivating inter-fraternal relationships, and empowering our member organizations.

clubs.name: Multicultural Innovators in Computer Sciences at University Park
clubs.summary: MICS aims to foster an inclusive environment for underrepresented groups in computer science, encouraging innovation, collaboration, and leadership development.
clubs.description: MICS (Multicultural Innovators in Computer Science) by ColorStack is dedicated to promoting diversity and inclusion in the field of computer science. Through technical workshops, mentorship, and leadership opportunities, we empower underrepresented students to achieve their fullest potential.

clubs.name: Multicultural Student Nursing Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Multicultural students in the college of nursing growing academically and forming a community to help each other succeed.
clubs.description: MSNA is an organization at Penn State that is dedicated to bringing together the diverse community of nursing students and creating a safe space for them. MSNA's goal is to help such students create community that will help them succeed as Nursing students. The organization offers mentoring and outreach throughout the year to current and incoming students. Events are held throughout the year to further strengthen the relationship students have with each other, as well as faculty members in the college.

clubs.name: Multicultural Undergraduate Law Association at University Park
clubs.summary: MULA's mission is to increase diversity in the field of law by promoting multiculturalism; to that end, we strive not only to help our members get into the law school of their choice but also to help our members succeed in the law school of their choice.

clubs.name: Multicultural Women's Association at University Park
clubs.summary: The Multicultural Women’s Association (MWA) supports multicultural women within and beyond the Smeal College of Business. We build community, leadership, and professional growth. We are businesswomen committed to addressing the unique cultural and gender
clubs.description: The Multicultural Women’s Association (MWA) supports multicultural women within and beyond the Smeal College of Business. We build community, leadership, and professional growth. We are businesswomen committed to addressing the unique cultural and gender experiences of women of color.

clubs.name: Murder Mystery Development Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of this organization shall be to plan, create, and host murder mystery events for Penn State students. The fall semester will be devoted to planning and creating, while the spring semester will be spent hosting these events.
clubs.description: The Murder Mystery Development Club, MMD, aims to develop creative, interactive, and exciting murder mystery scenarios based around immersive plots developed for students of Penn State University. Creativity is a cornerstone of the organization and is the focus of MMD.

clubs.name: Music Group at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Music Group at Penn State is Penn State's student-run mock record label, aspiring to create the music industry's next generations of leaders - whether those be artists, producers, businesspeople, or others. Come work with us!
clubs.description: Our mission is to create the music industry's next generation of leaders – whether that be artists, producers, businesspeople, or media specialists. At PSMG, students strive to push the music industry forward and find new ways to change the creative landscape. Ultimately, Music Group's vision is to bridge the gap between Penn State and the music industry. From our organization, students will develop project-centered experience across the practices of song creation, management, A&R, marketing, videography, and more. Music Group at Penn State is modeled from seasoned, industry-wide companies. Thus, we aim to garner attention from major music industry entities and see that our students find a career path that aligns with their creative passions. We not only want to enhance the music industry education available for students, but we aim to make Penn State a target for major music companies. One day, we hope to see companies like Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music Group, and more at Penn State career fairs. Through office visits, networking opportunities, and guest speaker events, we plan on building strong relationships and recruiting pipelines down the road.

clubs.name: Music Service Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Music Service Club's mission is to share the power of music with the State College community, especially the young, elderly, and disabled. We provide a welcoming space for students to continue music in college while giving back to the community.
clubs.description: Music Service Club was established in 2014 to bring the joy and healing power of music to the State College community. We visit groups in need across the State College area, bringing music into the lives of the young, elderly, disabled, and more. Students of all backgrounds and levels are welcome. We also welcome collaborations with other service and performing arts organizations on campus. Reach out if you have an idea and/or need our help! Find more information on our ManyBio!

clubs.name: Music Teachers National Association Collegiate Chapter at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of this organization is to advance the value and study of music-making to society and to support the professionalism of musicians. It is open to all Penn State University Students involved in regular music study.

clubs.description: Purpose: To foster a community-based mutual aid network among Muslim graduate and professional students at Penn State, sustained by the voluntary exchange of resources and services for mutual benefit. To foster discussions and intercultural dialogue and understanding between Muslim graduate and professional students from different disciplines, cultures and countries. To provide social, logistical, professional and academic support for incoming and continuing Muslim graduate and professional students at Penn State. To forge social and professional connections between Muslim graduate and professional students, and Muslim Penn State faculty, staff, alumni and undergraduate students. Current Activities: Aiding incoming students with settling in and housing arrangements. Community-building social and cultural activities Sharing community-created resources on organizational website. Future Activities: Conducting peer-organized writing workshops and peer-review sessions. Organizing professional and academic talks and roundtables by Muslim guest speakers from within and outside Penn State. Organizing workshops on issues pertaining to racial and religious discrimination and microagression i

clubs.name: Muslim Legal Society at Dickinson Law in UP

Our organization also seeks to educate the broader community about Islamic customs, traditions, and values, promoting understanding and inclusion within the legal profession.

clubs.summary: Promotes unity and join action among the Muslims, conducts various activities in the best traditions of Islam, promotes friendly relations between Muslims and non-Muslims, and makes Islamic teachings known to non-Muslims.

clubs.name: NABA: The Organization for Black Business Students at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of NABA: The Organization for Black Business Students involve supporting black students within the spectrum of business-related majors and economically empowering the black community at Penn State.

The Association shall unite through business related professionals and students who have similar interests and ideals, are committed to professional and academic excellence, possess a sense of professional and civic responsibility, and are concerned with enhancing opportunities for minorities in the business related professions.

clubs.name: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of the NAACP is to inform, eliminate race-based discrimination, fight for equality, and ensure the health and well-being of all persons.

We envision a liberated, inclusive society where every individual can fully exercise their civil and human rights free from discrimination. With more than 2 million members and 117 years of impact, we uplift underrepresented voices, advocate for justice, and drive meaningful change.

clubs.name: National Association of Black Journalists at University Park
clubs.summary: The Penn State chapter of the National Association of Black Journalists is a professional club for students of color interested in journalism, communications, and media to network and advance communication skills.
clubs.description: The Penn State chapter of NABJ pledges to strengthen ties among student journalists, Black journalists, journalism educators, and media professionals while strengthening students’ professional media etiquette for future opportunities. Students involved with NABJ will have the opportunity to listen to industry professionals speak, attend conferences, and work towards becoming more well rounded members of the media.

clubs.name: National Association of Home Builders at University Park
clubs.summary: NAHB Student Chapters is designed to help students gain a better understanding of the residential construction field through the use of guest lectures, meetings, and student competitions. All majors are welcome!

To unite non-profit organizations of women in a council of organizations primarily concerned with the welfare of Negro women. 3. To build cohesion between women through our shared similarities and distinct differences. 4. To devise ways to use each others' differences to enrich our vision and our joint struggles.

clubs.name: National Electrical Contractors Association at University Park
clubs.summary: To promote renewable energy system design, service learning, and electrical career opportunities through an industry-university partnership.
clubs.description: NECA aims to promote the electrical contracting industry within the university by presenting student members sustainable building design experience while connecting them with industry employers and enhancing their career opportunities.

clubs.summary: National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers Student Chapter at The Pennsylvania State University aims to foster a space where students of color in science, technology, and engineering are supported.
clubs.description: National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers (NOBCChE) Student Chapter at The Pennsylvania State University three main purposes: (1) to encourage the professional development of students of color in fields including, but not limited to science, technology, and engineering, (2) to provide academic and personal support to its members, and (3) to promote diversity among future professionals within these fields.

clubs.name: National Organization of Minority Architecture Students at University Park
clubs.summary: To foster communication, cooperation, solidarity and fellowship among minority students of architecture.
clubs.description: NOMAS is the student chapter of The National Organization of Minority Architects which on the national website states that they thrive only when voluntary members contribute their time and resources, has as its mission the building of a strong national organization, strong chapters, and strong members for the purpose of minimizing the effect of racism in our profession. We strive to do this through professional networking, community advocacy, and equitable design. Our goal is to educate our members to design with ethics, culture, economics, and systemic justice to improve our impact in human kind.

clubs.name: Nature and Art Rx at University Park
clubs.summary: Penn State's Nature and Art Rx program seeks to connect students, faculty, and staff with nature, art, and culture to improve community mental and physical well-being.
clubs.description: Penn State's Nature and Art Rx program seeks to connect students, faculty, and staff with nature, art, and culture to improve community mental and physical well-being. We aim to do so by providing awareness of opportunities to engage in artistic and natural spaces and by improving individual access to and comfort in these spaces. By partnering with Counseling and Psychological Services and University Health Services, students can expect to receive recommendations to connect with nature and art as part of a holistic approach to supporting well-being. Nature and Art Rx is a partnership between Student Affairs, Penn State Outreach, and the College of Arts and Architecture. Student Affairs is represented by staff from Campus Recreation, Counseling and Psychological Services, Health Promotion and Wellness, Student Arts Engagement, the Dr. Keiko Miwa Ross Student Farm, and University Health Services College of Arts and Architecture is represented by staff from The Palmer Art Museum Penn State Outreach is represented by staff from The Arboretum at Penn State and Shaver's Creek Environmental Center

The purpose of Natya is to provide for members an environment to foster their passion for these dance forms. We also strive to provide those new and unfamiliar to this dance form a basic understanding and appreciation of this art form. Natya allows members who are already experienced for a chance to explore their talent further, expand their knowledge, and perform the art at various cultural events. Fall 2026 Tryouts information will be posted on the Instagram @pennstatenatya

clubs.name: Navigators at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Penn State Navigators is a gospel centered community that is committed to knowing Christ, making him known on our campus, and seeing the gospel of Jesus transform lives! We would love to meet you and have you be a part of our community!
clubs.description: Penn State Navigators is a discipleship focused ministry with large group meetings every Friday and several Bible studies throughout the week. We value gospel-centered friendships, teaching, and mentorship with opportunities for growth, leadership, and service. Our biggest events are our Welcome Week activities, Fall Retreat, Winter Formal, Spring Break Service Trip, and our Spring Formal. Feel free to reach out with any questions or comments. We would love to connect!

clubs.name: Nepali Society at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: We seek to bring the wonderful members of our community together and share our culture with everyone at Penn State.
clubs.description: The purpose of Nepali Society at Penn State (herein referred as ‘NSPS') is to preserve and promote Nepali Culture, foster cooperation among all the individuals who share common interests about Nepal and its culture, and facilitate collaboration, entrepreneurial partnerships and exchange programs between Penn State and other private and public organizations, both within the USA and overseas.

clubs.name: Neurodiversity Alliance at University Park
clubs.summary: Neurodiversity Alliance PSU aims to provide an inclusive, close-knit community to all neurodivergent students and allies on campus, providing leadership, scholarship, and event opportunities to make their college experience more enjoyable.
clubs.description: Neurodiversity Alliance PSU is a expansion of the current Neurodiversity community partially supported by the SDR office. As a campus chapter of the national organization The Neurodiversity Alliance, we hope to utilize the fundings to provide students with learning disabilities and the allies a safe space to talk in, make connections, organize sensory-friendly events and give them the skill and opportunities to lead.

clubs.name: NeuroLion Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The mission of our organization to help undergraduate students gain exposure to the field of neuroscience. We will have guest speakers and explore current research and advancements in the neuroscience field in both industry and research. Come join us!

clubs.name: Neuroscience Club at World Campus
clubs.summary: Curious about the brain? The Neuroscience Club brings students together to explore neuroscience and the human brain through conversations, research, events, and shared curiosity. All majors welcome.
clubs.description: A student-led organization dedicated to building a vibrant, intellectually curious community for anyone interested in the brain, behavior, and the science of human experience. Open to all majors and backgrounds, the club provides an accessible, engaging space where students can explore neuroscience through discussion, research literacy, and meaningful academic connection. The club’s mission is to spark interest, grow scientific thinking, and expand opportunities for students across World Campus who want deeper exposure to neuroscience. Through journal clubs, discussions, occasional speakers, themed semesters, and student-led presentations, the organization creates structured yet welcoming avenues for students to learn, question, and develop confidence in engaging with neuroscience research.

clubs.name: New Life Student Fellowship at University Park
clubs.summary: Raising up servant leaders who live out their faith in Jesus to serve the Penn State campus, community, and beyond.
clubs.description: A student led ministry at Penn State where students journey together in their faith through the process of Reach, Disciple, and Send. Students grow personally in their walk with Christ and actively examine what it means to serve and love the Penn State community. If you want to learn more about Jesus, have a great family community, and have fun, this is the group for you!

clubs.name: New Wine Worship at University Park
clubs.summary: Our mission is to unite Christian organizations across campus so that students can connect with one another and build community in Christ through music, fellowship, and prayer. We also want to live out the gospel by reaching new students.
clubs.description: Our mission is to unite Christian organizations across campus so that students can connect with one another and build community in Christ through music, fellowship, and prayer. WE also want to live out the gospel by reaching new students who do not yet know Christ and are not yet connected to a fellowship community.

clubs.name: Newman Catholic Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Promotes, builds, and serves the developing University-Catholic community through religious, educational, and social activities, and encourages members to take an active role in the Church and secular society.
clubs.description: Newman creates an environment, through meetings, events, and activities, that is conducive to the spiritual, social, and intellectual growth of the undergraduate and graduate Catholic population at University Park. Faithful devotion to the teachings of the Roman Catholic Church, depth in prayer, growth in Christian virtue, radiation of charity, joy in fellowship, and active witness to the Truth are all ends that Newman hopes to foster in its members through Jesus Christ, with the active working of the Holy Spirit for the glory of God the Father. Attainment will strengthen and propel members towards sainthood and the beatific vision, thereby allowing for the sanctification of the world.

clubs.name: Next Generation Leadership Chapter at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Next Gen aims to inspire Penn State undergraduate students from all majors to explore public service careers and equip the next generation of civic leaders with the skills they need to make an impact in their communities and beyond.
clubs.description: The mission of this organization is to inspire Penn State undergraduate students from all majors to explore public service careers and equip the next generation of civic leaders with the skills they need to make an impact in their communities and beyond. As the world becomes more complex and the challenges we face are increasingly difficult to solve, now more than ever, we need talented civic leaders who are passionate about public service. The Next Gen Leadership Chapter is for Penn Staters who want to engage critically with the most important issues in society, those who are eager to make a difference, and those who want to lead by example. The organization seeks to empower students by helping them develop the skills, knowledge, and experience necessary to become part of the next generation of public service leaders who will tackle these issues head-on.

clubs.name: NextGen at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: WE ARE! NextGen at Penn State University, a chapter of NextGen America! NextGen America is the nation's largest youth voting advocacy group in the country, with its mission being to help young people register to vote and get involved in politics.
clubs.description: WE ARE! NextGen at Penn State University, a chapter of NextGen America! NextGen America is the nation's largest youth voting advocacy group in the country, with its mission being to help young people register to vote and get involved in politics. As a NextGen chapter, we further this mission at Penn State, helping college students get involved in politics and learn how and why to vote. Join us on our mission to empower young voters!

clubs.name: Nexus (Network for Excellence in Undergraduate Science) at University Park
clubs.summary: The Network for Excellence in Undergraduate Science serves to orient first year undergraduates to the Penn State University Park in the beginning of the fall and spring semesters. We hope to establish good connections with...
clubs.description: The Network for Excellence in Undergraduate Science serves to orient first year undergraduates to the Penn State University Park in the beginning of the fall and spring semesters. We hope to establish good connections with the students so we could later act as mentors and assist them with networking and academic development within the Eberly College of Science.

clubs.name: Nittany AI Student Society at University Park
clubs.summary: The Nittany AI Student Society seeks to engage and educate students on artificial intelligence and how it will affect their academic, professional, and entrepreneurial endeavors. We provide all opportunities for hands-on learning and experience building!
clubs.description: The Nittany AI Student Society aims to grow students to become leaders in technology. We do this by supporting the Nittany Ai Alliance in creating a community for all students passionate about Ai and providing them with a platform to grow their skills and apply them in real-world contexts. We host several programs designed to equip students with entrepreneurial and technical skills, including our annual Leadership Academy, which fosters essential entrepreneurship abilities, and our Machine Learning Bootcamp, where students gain practical expertise in AI. These initiatives help students effectively prepare for AI-focused opportunities like the Nittany AI Challenge and Nittany AI Advance. Active members of this club have participated in real-world problem solving, technical presentations, pitch competitions, and more… Join our organization to be a part of a like-minded community, that is passionate about growing in the Ai field and learning how to leverage it in any industry in today's world! Open to beginners and non-technical students (all majors are welcome)!

clubs.name: Nittany Chemical Society at University Park
clubs.summary: We provide a community for all majors with an interest in chemistry by doing outreach, attending conferences, and socializing!
clubs.description: Our student organization annually sends students to the national meeting of the American Chemical Society to present their research and network within the chemistry community. In addition, we do science outreach with local schools and programs as well as provide a community for chemistry majors and those interested in chemistry.

clubs.name: Nittany Dance Project at University Park
clubs.summary: Our purpose is to provide a space on the Penn State campus for students that have had extensive dance training wherein they can continue to practice, perform and enjoy all different genres of dance in one specific club.

clubs.name: Nittany Data Labs at University Park
clubs.summary: Student Organization focused on data science education, application, and community.
clubs.description: To provide students with the education, exposure, and experience with Data Science. Our club provides a comprehensive training program to teach and provide the tools and framework for students interested in better understanding Data Science - both in the fundamentals as well as the state-of-the-art techniques.

clubs.name: Nittany Divers SCUBA Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The Nittany Divers SCUBA Club is one of the oldest student organizations at Penn State! We are a dedicated group of students and faculty members that work to promote SCUBA diving and to spread the word on the importance of ocean conservation.
clubs.description: The Nittany Divers was founded to promote and to encourage SCUBA diving in a safe and sensible manner. We serve to encourage and to promote the underwater world, including oceanography, marine biology, and archeology, to provide a common meeting ground for all those interested in any phase of SCUBA diving. Furthermore, we hold the responsibility of assuming the sponsorship of social events among persons interested in SCUBA diving, such as guest speakers, social gatherings, and SCUBA trips

clubs.name: Nittany Entrepreneur Society at University Park
clubs.summary: NES is an entrepreneurial and intrapreneurial community dedicated to connecting people with their passions, exposing them to new ideas, and challenging what is possible.
clubs.description: Nittany Entrepreneur Society, formerly known as Innoblue, is the oldest entrepreneurial organization on campus; it was created before Invent Penn State when there was very little entrepreneurship infrastructure on campus. This organization is responsible for creating the Summer Founders Program, HackPSU, LionLaunch Pad, Blockchain Club, and several other technology and entrepreneurship initiatives at Penn State. To this day, we remain committed to the ideas of innovation and entrepreneurship that we were founded on. Still, we are adapting as the needs of the university are constantly changing. We want to expose students to new ideas/opportunities while educating them about many recent topics to connect them with their passions earlier in their college careers. We accomplish these goals by organizing events such as the start-up career fair and our signature speaker series, hosting workshops to help improve the skills and knowledge of the student body, and providing support/opportunities for student-led projects to encourage people to apply their skills/talents. That being said, there is room for every type of person to find a role within Nittany Entrepreneur Society.

clubs.name: Nittany Gaffer's Guild at University Park

clubs.name: Nittany Lion Careers
Nittany Motorsports at University Park
clubs.summary: Here at University Park, we compete in the world's largest collegiate design series: Formula SAE/Formula Student. If you're interested in joining, come check us out in the Engineering Services Building or check our website and social media for updates.
clubs.description: Nittany Motorsports provides its members opportunities to gain broader insight into the engineering and business professions by sponsoring various automotive-related activities and competitions. The University Park chapter only consists of the Formula SAE/Formula Student competition, run and organized out of the Competition Team Garage in the Engineering Services Building. Nittany Motorsports is a student-run design team tasked with designing and prototyping a formula-style race car for the annual Formula SAE/Formula Student competitions. At these competitions, teams from all over the world are judged in both static and dynamic events including cost of production, ergonomics, investment, acceleration, skidpad, autocross, and an endurance race. The competition provides students with an opportunity to apply their engineering, design, and communication skills in a professional setting. For more information about Nittany Motorsports, check out our LinkTree: https://linktr.ee/psfr. It has all of our socials and our Microsoft Teams, where all our internal communication happens.

clubs.name: Nittany Neuroscience Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Nittany Neuroscience Club is a club dedicated to anyone who has in interest in the field of neuroscience or neurology. We are dedicated to promote interest in the field of neuroscience and expand its discoveries to the public.

clubs.name: Nittany Recreational Curling League at University Park

clubs.name: No Refund Theatre at University Park
clubs.summary: Provides opportunities for all students, regardless of major, to perform, direct, write and produce all types of theatre.
clubs.description: No Refund Theatre is a student-run theatre organization at Penn State University that strives to perform numerous theatrical performances each semester, completely free of charge. (Hence why we give no refunds!) The purpose of NRT is to give all students, regardless of major, the opportunity to perform, direct, and produce all types of theatre. We perform a range of theatrical shows all in 111 Forum. Our shows are completely student-run, from our actors, tech, directors, and in some instances, the writers! Club theatre is what keeps the arts alive in many of our lives, therefore we strive to create a welcoming, inclusive, and safe environment to share our love for the arts here on campus.

No prior experience is needed to join these workshops. Open practice hours are held weekly at the HUB. Please reach out to us for questions about membership, opportunities or events! clubs.name: Nuclear Navy Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Penn State Nuclear Navy Club is an academic club created by Penn State NROTC which allows students to explore the nuclear pathways available through the United States Navy, as well as promote a higher academic understanding of math and physics.
clubs.description: The Penn State Nuclear Navy Club is an academic club created by Penn State NROTC which allows students to explore the nuclear pathways available through the United States Navy, as well as promote a higher academic understanding of math and physics.

clubs.summary: Promotes cohesiveness and communication among graduate students in the various departments within the Interdepartmental Graduate Program in Nutrition and promotes a free exchange of information.

clubs.name: NWTF Spur Collectors - Penn State Chapter at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of the NWTF Spur Collectors - Penn State Chapter is support the conservation of the wild turkey and preserve the hunting heritage of Pennsylvania Sportsmen.
clubs.description: WE ARE the first collegiate chapter of the National Wild Turkey Federation in Pennsylvania! While we're affiliated with the NWTF, our general focus is on the overall conservation of wild species and habitats and the recruitment of young people in the outdoors! We host several events throughout the year, including but not limited to, group hunts and fishing trips, range days, presentations from biologist and conservation professionals, and group trips to places like Benezette, PA to see the native elk herd, and Nashville, Tennessee for the NWTF's national convention. We consider ourselves a pretty laid back club that enjoys spending time in the great outdoors and having a great time while doing it. We're always open to new ideas and new friendly faces! If you have any questions or are interested in joining, please don't hesitate to email our President, Sarah, at ses6659@psu.edu.

clubs.name: Oboe Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The Oboe Club at Penn State University Park provides enriching opportunities for oboists of all levels, including student music majors and non-majors, in a welcoming community at Penn State University Park.
clubs.description: The mission of the Oboe Club at Penn State University Park is to provide enriching opportunities for oboists of all levels in a welcoming community at Penn State University Park. The Oboe Club at Penn State University Park serves as a forum for oboists to share work in progress, techniques, ideas, and resources in an open and non-discriminatory manner. This club seeks to raise awareness of the oboe's importance in modern music, which includes presenting or sponsoring recitals and masterclasses with esteemed oboists from around the world. The Oboe Club at Penn State University Park encourages participation from oboists from across the campus, including music majors and non-majors.

clubs.name: Occupational Therapy Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To inform students interested in occupational therapy about opportunities for graduate school and other future endeavors.
clubs.description: The Occupational Therapy Club is a student organization for Penn State students who are considering a career in occupational therapy. In order to fully enlighten students about this field and the process of applying to graduate school, our club members participate in a wide range of meetings and events: informational sessions led by the executive team, Zoom calls with graduate school admissions officers, Zoom calls with students currently in graduate school, and community service activities. The OT Club is a great way to connect with other students interested in this career.

clubs.name: Off-Campus Student Support
clubs.summary: Off-Campus Student Support, within the Office of Student Care & Advocacy, is a unit within Student Affairs. We offer support to students who live off-campus or are preparing to live off-campus.

clubs.name: Office of Science Engagement
clubs.summary: asdf
clubs.description: The Office of Science Engagement is composed of three different branches: Undergraduate research, professional development, and education abroad. We are all dedicated to helping students like you graduate with both a diploma and a resume, full of value and experience.

clubs.name: Ohana at University Park
clubs.summary: To provide fundraising opportunities and create awareness for the Penn State student body in support of the Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance MaraTHON.
clubs.description: Ohana's mission is to provide Penn State students with an opportunity to raise money and lend support to Four Diamonds families who are part of the Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance Marathon (THON). Ohana aims to create an inclusive and close-knit community of friends dedicated to this common goal. Ohana members bring love, support, determination and strength to those children suffering from pediatric cancer and become a family away from home for them to turn to, creating memories that will last a lifetime for all involved.

clubs.name: Omani Student Association at University Park

clubs.name: Omega Chi Epsilon at University Park
clubs.summary: The Pennsylvania State University is proud to be the Beta Alpha Chapter of Omega Chi Epsilon, the chemical engineering honor society. The organization provides high scholarship opportunities and promotes student-faculty connections.
clubs.description: Omega Chi Epsilon is the Honor Society for Chemical Engineering. The Society promotes high scholarship, encourages original investigation in chemical engineering, and recognizes the valuable traits of character, integrity, and leadership. It serves both undergraduate and graduate students and fosters meaningful student-faculty dialogue. The name is based upon our motto: Ode Chrototos Eggegramai which means In this Society, professionalism is engraved in our minds. The letters OXE, or their Greek equivalent of WCE, represent Order of Chemical Engineers. The key (see image above) represents the objectives of Omega Chi Epsilon. The four arms of the Maltese cross represent the first four objectives: RECOGNITION to recognize excellence in chemical engineering, INVESTIGATION to promote original investigation and innovation in chemical engineering, SERVICE to provide service to the chemical engineering department or school and its student body, COMRADESHIP to promote comradeship among chemical engineers These four are bound intimately together by the fifth, and PROFESSIONALISM to promote honesty, integrity, and social responsibility: the hallmarks of professional ethics Represented by the

clubs.name: Omega Chi Sigma at University Park
clubs.summary: Omega Chi Sigma is a co-ed preparatory professional fraternity. Its focus is on the interrelationship between the business world and the world of science, technology, engineering, and math-related fields.
clubs.description: Omega Chi Sigma is a co-ed preparatory professional fraternity. Its focus is on the interrelationship between the business world and the world of science, technology, engineering, and math-related fields. The purpose of this organization is to provide opportunities for both business and non-business-related majors to better develop skills necessary for success in a professional business setting. We celebrate the need for cooperation and teamwork between those of all majors and career paths at Penn State University.

clubs.name: Omega Delta Sigma at University Park
clubs.summary: The Penn State Military and Veterans Fraternity Omega Delta Sigma exists to enhance the lives of veterans and the surrounding community through outreach, philanthropy, social events, and volunteering.
clubs.description: ODS exists to provide veterans and military members attending school with the opportunity to network with other military members, help with the transition process, student leadership positions, community volunteering, professional networking as well as providing the opportunity to socialize with other veteran and military students.

clubs.name: Omega Phi Alpha at University Park
clubs.summary: Omega Phi Alpha is a National Service sorority and an associate chapter of the Penn State Panhellenic Council. Omega Phi Alpha was founded on the principles of friendship, leadership and service.
clubs.description: Omega Phi Alpha is a National Service sorority and an associate chapter of the Penn State Panhellenic Council. Omega Phi Alpha was founded on the principles of friendship, leadership and service. We have 6 main areas of service including members of the sorority, university community, community at large, nations of the world, presidents project and mental health which is our permanent project. We participate in many of the same activities as other Panhellenic Sororities here at Penn State, including Homecoming, Greek Week and THON, while also actively participating in service projects benefiting the Penn State community and beyond. Omega Phi Alpha has a close, family feel that is hard to find anywhere else. Our commitment to service and to our sisterhood creates an experience that will enrich our lives for years to come.

clubs.name: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. at University Park
clubs.summary: Omega Psi Phi is a non profit organization founded on the Cardinal Principles of Manhood, Scholarship, Perseverance, and Uplift. We are seeking to engage our communities through service, social action, and projects.

clubs.name: Open Build Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To develop and strengthen student technical ability through the collaborative design and execution of engineering projects. We are committed to open-source, ensuring all works are documented and published for free for all to recreate and expand upon.
clubs.description: The Open build Club is an engineering club that focuses on open-source or documenting and publishing projects freely to the public to use and change. normally it is seen a lot in software, but we want to bring it to all disciplines of engineering. normally the motivators for open-source projects are affordability, accessibility, education, autonomy, or simply just someone is passionate about it. the club tries to build projects off that idea, to contribute to the existing community, while also building our own technical skills.

clubs.name: Operation Blue and Gold at University Park
clubs.summary: To give Naval ROTC students the opportunity to support the mission of the Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance Marathon and enhance the lives of children and families impacted by childhood cancer.

clubs.name: Opulence: Drag Ambassadors at Penn State University Park

clubs.name: Orchesis Dance Company at University Park
clubs.summary: Penn State's oldest dance company thats specializes in contemporary and jazz styles. Dancers who come from a competitive and technical background can continue their training with us!
clubs.description: Orchesis Dance Company is a performing dance company consisting of about thirty dancers and has been around since 1935, making us the oldest dance company on campus! clubs.description: The Peruvian Student Association was born out of the need to give representation, a voice, to Peruvian Students at Penn State. This organization has three main goals: The primary goal of The Peruvian Student Association is to bring together Peruvian Students, as well as anyone interested in the Peruvian culture, and give them a sense of community, a place in which they can both share their cultures with each other, and transmit it with others. This organization would be a way to represent the body of Peruvian students, and to give a sense of validation to Peruvian traditions outside of Peru. The secondary focus of this organization is expressing, and helping to preserve the Peruvian culture. Through meetings as well as bigger events, the organization aims to educate not only it's members, but any student at Penn State, about the culture, ethics, entertainment, language, gastronomy, sociopolitical events, and history of Peru. Lastly, the organization hopes to help incoming Peruvian students, both graduate and undergraduate, to have a support system, a place to seek help in case of there being difficulties in adjusting to the culture lived in the US.

Red/blue teaming is a structured analytical exercise used to evaluate and improve an organization's defenses. The red team acts as adversaries or attackers, tasked with identifying vulnerabilities and attempting to breach systems, processes, or physical locations. The blue team represents the defenders, responsible for detecting, responding to, and mitigating the red team's attacks. We aim to be a fun way to immerse our members into the professional fields of healthcare and human services! Join us today!

clubs.name: Relay for Life at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Relay for Life at Penn State is a national collaboration of college students, faculty and staff dedicated to fighting cancer, volunteering for the American Cancer Society, and improving college communities.
clubs.description: The mission of Relay For Life at Penn State is to honor, support, and engage the cancer community in the University Park/State College, PA area by planning, promoting, and executing a 12-hour walk-a-thon, Relay For Life, benefitting the American Cancer Society. We are dedicated to celebrating, remembering, and fighting back in all that we do while working toward a world without cancer. You can learn more about our organization and how to get involved by visiting our social media accounts or emailing us!

clubs.name: Remedy Sports Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Remedy Sports club is about youth sports and the growing referee/official shortage across the US. A group of college students interested in sports or sports officiating coming together to understand the problem and proactively raise awareness/solutions.
clubs.description: The Remedy Sports club relates to youth sports and the growing referee/official shortage across the United States. It involves a group of college students interested in sports or sports officiating coming together to understand the problem and proactively raise awareness/solutions. The club often collaborates with Remedy Inc. which is an up-and-coming company driven to solve the official shortage utilizing innovative tech-driven solutions.

clubs.name: Remote Area Medical at University Park
clubs.summary: We volunteer at popup clinics and run our own annual popup clinic. All provide free, quality healthcare (dental, medical, and vision) to underserved communities. This opportunity is particularly valuable for aspiring health professionals.
clubs.description: Are you interested in medicine or service? Do you want to help provide healthcare to underserved populations, alongside a supportive community of Penn State students? Penn State Remote Area Medical (RAM) would love to have you! Penn State RAM is a college chapter of the national nonprofit Remote Area Medical, which hosts health clinics across the country to provide free, quality healthcare to those in need. Our chapter supports this goal by volunteering at RAM clinics in Pennsylvania and neighboring states, while also enriching students' experiences with workshops and resources. Here in Centre County, we also host our own annual RAM clinic! Our 2026 clinic served 171 patients $132,496 in free services. Our organization led the efforts of recruiting medical professionals, promoting the event, organizing food for over 200 volunteers, and establishing the venue. For more details about Penn State RAM, visit our website or contact efb5543@psu.edu. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OEQA8RSvfbs&t=80s

clubs.name: Renaissance Faire Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The PSU Renaissance Faire Club is dedicated to fostering a vibrant community that celebrates creativity, history, and the arts. We aim to inspire members through engaging events, immersive experiences, and hope to run a faire during the spring semester.
clubs.description: The Penn State Renaissance Faire Club is dedicated to fostering a vibrant community that celebrates creativity, history, and the arts. We aim to inspire members through engaging events, immersive experiences, and educational opportunities, all while promoting inclusivity and collaboration. Together, we bring the spirit of the Renaissance to life, enriching the Penn State experience and encouraging a deeper appreciation for the diverse cultures and traditions of the past. We hope to revitalize the club and hold a faire during the spring semester.

clubs.name: Reproductive Justice Project at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: The RJP is a hub for all things reproductive justice (RJ) at Penn State, housed within the WGSS Dept. Our purpose is to advance RJ efforts at Penn State, particularly through promoting RJ and RJ-related education, events, programs, and organizations.
clubs.description: The Reproductive Justice Project at Penn State (PSURJP) is a student organization dedicated to advancing reproductive justice efforts at Penn State through education, discussion, collaboration, and community engagement. We promote educational opportunities, partner with organizations with similar goals, and host events centered around reproductive justice and broader healthcare equity issues. In all of our work, we honor the four tenets of reproductive justice: the right to have children, the right not to have children, the right to parent in safe and sustainable communities, and the right to maintain personal bodily autonomy. We also recognize and celebrate the history of the reproductive justice movement and framework, which was founded by Black women and is rooted in addressing systemic inequities in healthcare and society. Our organization welcomes anyone interested in reproductive justice, healthcare disparities, public health, ethics, policy, advocacy, or the ways these issues shape people's lives and communities. Whether you are deeply involved in these topics or simply interested in learning more, we encourage you to join us! For more information, please contact Nevaeh Sick

clubs.name: Residence Life - Living Learning Communities
clubs.summary: Connect with the staff for the Residence Life Living Learning Communities at PSU University Park!
clubs.description: The mission of the Living Learning Community program is to cultivate multi-faceted communities that enhance student learning through academic partnerships; value individual and collective diversity; and support student transition and personal growth while fostering responsible citizenship. This space is for all our faculty, staff, and student leaders involved with LLCs to have access to important updates, be able to RSVP for events, and request funding for their LLC activities. LLC Learning Outcomes Every person will be able to develop competency in building and maintaining community in which they want to engage; Every person will be able to feel empowered to understand and analyze their own experiences, goals, and identities; Every person will be able to develop skills and strategies to pursue academic endeavors that are meaningful to them. Penn State Student Affairs: Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. Student Affairs is committed to building a community of belonging for all.

clubs.name: Revive at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Revive is a Jesus-centered campus ministry at Penn State. We are real people doing real life together, & we are intent on adopting everyone into the family of faith by showing them their value as children of God.
clubs.description: Revive is a Jesus-centered campus ministry at Penn State. We are real people doing real life together, & we are intent on adopting everyone into the family of faith by showing them their value as children of God. We are connected to the Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod. To be Lutheran simply means that we accept the scriptural truths that inspired the reformation of the Christian Church in the 16th century and led to a renewed focus on the Gospel. Locally, we are a part of the church, Good Shepherd Evangelical Lutheran.

clubs.name: Rewrite at University Park
clubs.summary: The Rewrite is a literary community that explores diverse voices and stories, particularly those centered on women of color. Through reading, discussion, and community-building, members engage with literature that fosters representation empathy community
clubs.description: The Rewrite is a student-led literary organization dedicated to creating an inclusive and engaging space for readers who are interested in learning and experiencing storytelling through a diverse lens and exploring how different perspectives can transform the reading experience. Inspired by the impact of seeing oneself represented in literature, The Rewrite focuses on exploring books and narratives that highlight the experiences, cultures, and perspectives of women of color and other underrepresented communities. Through book discussions, literary events, community-building activities, and thoughtful conversations, members are encouraged to engage with stories that broaden perspectives, foster empathy, and celebrate diverse voices. The organization aims to create a welcoming environment where students can connect through a shared love of reading while developing a deeper appreciation for literature and the power of storytelling. Membership is open to all Penn State students regardless of major, background, or previous literary experience. clubs.summary: Rhythm Gaming Club - Dance Dance Maniacs is a club devoted to promoting physical activity and entertainment via dance simulation video games similar to Konami's Dance Dance Revolution series and various other rhythm games.

clubs.name: Roar Zone at University Park
clubs.summary: The Roar Zone is the official student section of Penn State Men's and Women's Ice Hockey. Our mission is to provide an exciting, positive, and supportive atmosphere inside Pegula Ice Arena.
clubs.description: Embodied by over a thousand passionate students, the Roar Zone pulsates as the very heartbeat of Hockey Valley, igniting sheer exhilaration in every corner of Pegula Ice Arena. Renowned as the #1 student section in college hockey, we infuse each match with a surge of electricity that is simply unmatched. Since our inception in 2013, The Roar Zone has served as the thunderous roar behind every Penn State men's and women's hockey showdown at Pegula. With dynamic chants, vibrant songs, dazzling posters, creative props, themed extravaganzas, and our iconic cowbell, we transform Pegula into a cauldron of unmatched spirit and noise. Always at the forefront of innovation, we eagerly embrace new trends and ideas, welcoming all suggestions with open arms! Eager to become a part of the best atmosphere in college hockey? Reach out to us and discover how you can dive headfirst into the Roar Zone experience! Don't forget to follow us on Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok for a behind-the-scenes look at all the action!

clubs.name: Robo X at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of this club is to encourage engineering personal project and competition. The club's currently major purpose is to organize, prepare, and enter the Robomaster competition.
clubs.description: We are a team at Pennsylvania State University that focuses on Robotics research and development. As the only student organization to focus on R&D relating to robotics at Penn State, we are formed by veterans from international robotics competition such as DJI Robomaster. Gathering graduate and undergraduate students from colleges ranging from College of Engineering, Eberly College of Science, to Smeal College of Business, we are passionate about robotics, and grow under the objective of "we make things."

clubs.name: Robot in 3 Days at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Robot in 3 Days (Ri3D) at Penn State prepares for and hosts an annual build event to design and construct a functional competitive-concept FIRST Robotics Competition robot in 72 hours!
clubs.description: Robot in 3 Days (Ri3D) at Penn State prepares for and hosts an annual build event to design, construct, document, and publish a functional competitive-concept FIRST Robotics Competition robot in 72 hours!

clubs.name: Robotics Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Robotics Club focuses on the design, fabrication, and deployment of Arduino autonomous robots. In the club, members can learn about programming, design, and modern manufacturing tools such as 3D printing.
clubs.description: Robotics Club is a student-run organization on campus that meets weekly in the Engineering Services Building. Students learn about designing robots in a team environment, programming Arduino microcontrollers, and building autonomous robots for competitions. The club welcomes engineering and computer science majors as well as students seeking other degrees, as employers are seeking more of these advanced skills in the job market. In addition to club meetings, the club may offer information sessions from various employers, such as General Motors, and traditionally seeks applicants for a resume pool. We are also involved in building a 30lb battlebot for external competitions! For more information, please refer to our website. Click here to get involved!

clubs.name: Rock n' Roar: Popular Music Club at University Park
clubs.summary: Rock n' Roar is a PSU School of Music affiliated organization for students looking for a place to play and enjoy popular music with modern genres including rock, pop, and metal with like-minded creative peers.
clubs.description: Rock n' Roar is a place to explore, share, and appreciate the impact of popular music throughout the 20th century to now. Across a range of genres such as rock, pop, and metal, we aim to immerse ourselves in both technical and musical aspects as well as the values of expression and cultural context. Rock n’ Roar is unique in how it allows popular music to be approached with a sophistication that is rarely recognized by traditional music institutions. It bridges gaps between eras of musical expression, opening the floor for conversation and collaboration between music lovers of all disciplines and backgrounds. Additionally, the club helps to organize and promote local music performances and opportunities.

clubs.name: Rotaract Club at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: Rotaract brings together people to exchange ideas with leaders in the community, develop leadership and professional skills, and have fun through community service.
clubs.description: Rotaract focuses on young adults' development as leaders in their communities and workplaces. Clubs also take part in international service projects, in a global effort to bring peace and international understanding to the world. "Rotaract" stands for "Rotary in Action", although the name originally comes from a combination of "Rotary" and "Interact" (International + Action) Most Rotaract activities take place at the club level. Rotaract clubs hold formal meetings in person or virtually, usually every two weeks, that feature speakers, special outings, social activities, discussions, or visits to other clubs. Club members get together on designated days for service project work, social events, or professional/leadership development workshops. To be eligible for membership, you must be 18 years of age and show that you are committed to Rotaract and of good standing in your community. After being approved by the club, members are inducted into Rotaract. Avenues of service include Club Service, Community Service, International Service and Professional Development.

clubs.description: The Reserve Officer Training Corp Living Learning Community (ROTC LLC) is a first-year community located in Pennypacker Hall, East Residence Halls. Members participate in weekly events in the hall, as well as planning events around annual ROTC programs, such as wilderness training or regular PT exercises. Our events and programs are open to all students regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, or any other protected class. clubs.name: Rubik's Cube Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The Rubik's Cube Club was made to welcome beginners who are interested in learning to solve the Rubik's cube, and experienced solvers who want an environment to learn and compete against others.
clubs.description: Fall 2026 Meetings: Fridays 5:30 - 6:30 pm, Thomas 125 This club was created for people all across the spectrum of speed solving! If you are someone who has no prior experience in solving the Rubik's cube this club can teach you (it's not as hard as it looks). On the other hand if you are someone who is experienced in speed solving we will hold miniature competitions so you can test your skills against other group members. Finally if you are somewhat experienced but want to become faster, we can show walk-through solves and advanced tips. This club does not focus mainly on the well known 3x3 cube but rather on any form of puzzle similar to it. This includes "cubes" from 2x2... to ...7x7 and greater. Also included are "cubes" like the Skewb, Square-1, and Pyraminx. Feel free to bring any cubes you have to club meetings. The officers will also provide cubes to use at meetings as well. Join our GroupMe Instagram: @PennStateCube Website: https://sites.psu.edu/rubikscubeclub/

clubs.name: Run for the Cure at Penn State University Park
clubs.summary: We are a passionate group of Penn State students dedicated to organizing events and initiatives that bring people together in support of breast cancer research, awareness, and a better tomorrow.
clubs.description: Our mission is to unite the Penn State community in the fight against breast cancer by raising awareness and funds to support the Susan G. Komen Breast Cancer Foundation. Through year-round fundraising efforts and our on-campus runs, we aim to inspire hope, foster community, and make a meaningful impact in the lives of those affected by breast cancer. Join us in our commitment to making a difference, one step at a time!

clubs.name: Russian Studies Club at University Park
clubs.summary: The Russian Studies Club aims to create a network to facilitate communication among students in different years and, beyond that, to get in touch with alumni of the Russian studies in the Department of Germanic and Slavic Languages and Literatures.
clubs.description: The Russian Studies Club at Penn State is a student association that works in close collaboration with the Department of Germanic and Slavic Languages and Literatures. Our goal is to facilitate and expand students' knowledge of the Russian language and to explore, understand, and critically reassess the phenomenon of Russian culture in the face of Russia's war against Ukraine, which we unequivocally condemn (see https://german.la.psu.edu/news/statement-regarding-the-war-in-ukraine/). We welcome all members of the Penn State community to join us in this critical reassessment. The purpose of the Russian Studies Club is to create a network to facilitate communication among students interested in Russian language and culture and, beyond that, to get in touch with alumni of Russian studies in the Department of Germanic and Slavic Languages and Literature. We have weekly meetings called Russian Tea Hour, where we serve treats and dedicate time to various activities such as conversation practice, games, presentations by club members and invited speakers. We also organize various events such as Russian movie nights, field trips, and guest lecture events.

clubs.name: Rêve Dance Company at University Park

We hold auditions at the beginning of every fall semester. If you are interested in joining our team, please reach out on instagram: @revedancecopsu Everyone is welcome!!! :)

clubs.name: School of Hospitality Management THON Committee at University Park
clubs.summary: The purpose of SHM THON is to represent the students in the School of Hospitality Management in Penn State's Dance Marathon. We serve as the voice for every student majoring in Hospitality Management who hopes to get involved with THON.
clubs.description: The School of Hospitality Management THON Organization is a general organization within the Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance Marathon. THON is committed to enhancing the lives of children and families impacted by childhood cancer. Our mission is to support these families and raise awareness to promote funding for the Four Diamond Foundation in hopes of a cure. Throughout the year, SHM THON plans and executes fundraisers (dinners, pie your professor, and more!), and sends letters (THONvelopes) asking for donations to help raise money to help fight pediatric cancer.

clubs.name: School of International Affairs Black Student Association at University Park
clubs.summary: Organization for Black Students at the School of International Affairs designed to increase diversity and inclusion, highlight black contributions in foreign policy, and raise awareness for issues facing minorities at the School of International Affairs.
clubs.description: The purpose of the School of International Affairs Black Student Association (SIABSA) is to recruit, retain, and support Black and diaspora students at the School of International Affairs (SIA). We hope that through frequent meetings, speaking, and social events, and professional development opportunities, we can build a community within SIA. Aditionally, we hope to continue our work in connecting students with alumni and professors throughout the University Park campus

clubs.name: School of International Affairs Student Government Association at University Park

clubs.name: School of Theatre Benefitting THON at University Park
clubs.summary: SOT THON gives School of Theatre students the opportunity to be involved in Penn State's THON in a way that is conducive to their rehearsal and class schedules.
clubs.description: SOT THON is for all undergraduate School of Theatre students, including those pursuing theatre minors. This organization allows students to be involved in Penn State's THON, the largest student-run philanthropy in the world, in a way that is conducive to their rigorous rehearsal and class schedules each semester. We host unique special events and fundraisers to encourage involvement and raise money for families impacted by pediatric cancer. Our mission is to make every child feel like a star!

clubs.name: School of Theatre Student Diversity Committee at University Park
clubs.summary: As an organized body of student advocates and allies, the mission of the School of Theater Student Diversity Committee is to support the development of an inclusive culturally pluralistic environment and advocate for diversity, equity, and inclusion.

clubs.name: School of Visual Arts Black Indigenous and People of Color at University Park
clubs.summary: The organization's mission is to provide students interested in the various visual mediums of art with opportunities for creative development, student collaboration, community building, and opportunities that art students can put on their resumes.
clubs.description: The mission of the organization is to provide students interested in the various visual mediums of art with opportunities for creative development, student collaboration, and community building. Particular emphasis is placed on members having the benefit of working closely with other students of similar backgrounds and expertise. Supported by a diverse and inclusive environment, resources and assistance will be provided for members interested in professional and/or academic growth within the field of visual arts to initiate greater student empowerment and engagement.

clubs.name: School of Visual Arts Graduate Art Society at University Park
clubs.summary: The Graduate Art Society (G.A.S.) supports SoVA graduate students by creating opportunities for research, exhibition, collaboration, and professional development to enrich artistic practice inside and outside the studio.
clubs.description: The purpose of the Graduate Art Society (G.A.S.) is to support graduate students in the School of Visual Arts (SoVA) by fostering artistic research, professional development, collaboration, and community through exhibitions, events, publications, printed booklets, and shared opportunities beyond coursework.

clubs.name: Schreyer Consulting Group at University Park
clubs.summary: A Schreyer Honors College organization preparing students for careers in Management, Technology, and Strategy Consulting.
clubs.description: A consulting organization linked with Schreyer Honors College. Offers professional development, interview preparation, unique networking events, and fosters a community of high performing individuals who are interested in consulting.

clubs.name: Schreyer for Women at University Park
clubs.summary: A community within the Schreyer Honors College that focuses on empowering our scholars through professional and academic development, service events, community engagement programming, and creative special projects.
clubs.description: Schreyer for Women is an organization created in 2017 within the Schreyer Honors College that focuses on empowering our Scholars and surrounding communities. The foundation of this organization is built upon four pillars: Community Engagement, Career Development, Service, and Special Projects. These pillars provide a foundation for vibrant programming and provide spaces for Scholars to network, collaborate, learn, flourish, and contribute to their local and international communities while at Penn State and beyond. Our mission is to engage students in the SHC community at Penn State through events meant to bring focus to, and alleviate barriers to female-identifying individuals' potential in both our local and global communities. This is accomplished through the creation of networks and thought processes meant to help members reach their potential professionally; the organization of service events surrounding the empowerment of women; and the coordination of social events aimed at strengthening relationships within the community.

clubs.name: Schreyer Honors College
Schreyer Honors College Student Council at University Park
clubs.summary: Serves as a communication link between faculty, Schreyer Scholars, SHC administration, Living Learning Community, other college student councils, and SHC student orgs. Is comprised of 5 committees: social, service, merch, sustainability, and THON.
clubs.description: Schreyer Honors College Student Council serves as a communication link between university faculty, Schreyer Scholars, SHC administration, special interest housing, other college student councils, and SHC student orgs to coordinate student programming, service, THON, academic, professional, and social events. Additionally, the SHC Student Council designs and sells all Schreyer Honors College merchandise. The main goal of the SHC Student Council is to help foster and build relationships within the Schreyer community. General body meetings are Tuesdays at 7PM in the Grandfather Clock Lounge in Atherton Hall unless communicated otherwise. In addition to attending GBM's, you can get involved by joining one or more of our five committees (Social, Service, Sustainability, THON, and Merchandise)!

clubs.name: Schreyer Medical Team at University Park
clubs.summary: The Schreyer Medical Team plans and hosts informational healthcare related events including speaker series and trips to nearby medical schools.
clubs.description: The SMT is dedicated to fostering a community of prehealth students within the Schreyer Honors College. Through planned informational career events and immersive treks to esteemed medical schools, we strive to inspire, educate, and connect aspiring healthcare professionals. Our mission is to cultivate a supportive environment that nurtures passion, fosters academic and professional growth, and ultimately empowers our members to pursue impactful careers in medicine and allied health fields.

clubs.name: Science and the Bible Club at University Park
clubs.summary: To research the relationships between Science and the Bible and to educate others regarding these relationships.
clubs.description: Science & the Bible Club (SciBle) is a group of Bible-believing scientists, students and academics who believe that Christianity and science can (and do!) work together. In many college environments, religion and science cannot be openly discussed, even though there are many Bible-believing science professors & science majors. It's a tricky thing. We created SciBle for those who want to dig deeper into how Science and the Christian Bible relate.

clubs.name: Science Lionpride at University Park
clubs.summary: The ambassador organization for the Eberly College of Science. Providing insight to prospective students; connecting with Eberly College of Science Alumni; giving back to the Penn State and State College community.
clubs.description: Science Lionpride's mission is to serve as ambassadors to the Eberly College of Science, provide club members with professional development opportunities, to connect and involve the current Penn State community with its vast alumni association, and to promote philanthropy by facilitating service and school spirit. clubs.name: Soil Judging Team at University Park
clubs.summary: A soil judger will use their knowledge of soil to accurately determine morphological features found throughout the soil profile.
clubs.description: The Soil Judging is an Academic Team, not a club; we meet once or twice a year for a soil judging event held regionally, and if we qualify, nationally. A student participating in a soil judging academic contest will use their knowledge of soil to accurately determine morphological features found throughout the soil profile. The Soil Judging Academic Team has participated in the Northeast Regional Contest each Fall since the 1950s and, when qualifying, in the National Collegiate Contest each Spring. The contests are a part of the Soil Science Society of America's commitment to soil education. Students are provided the unique opportunity to see new soils, test their skills against their peers from across the country, and connect with professionals in the field. Students will also meet faculty that they may wish to study under in graduate school. Soil judging has had a long history of building professional skills in field classification with Penn State students. Past team members go on to be engineers, career soil scientists, professors, etc. The team meets biweekly in the Fall for practice before the contest in early October (typically).

clubs.description: The Bachelor of Science in Systems Neuroscience provides a rigorous interdisciplinary foundation in the study of the nervous system. Students will explore how the brain and nervous system function at all levels, from molecules and cells to behavior, cognition, and disease. Core coursework covers fundamental principles of neuroscience, including cellular and molecular neurobiology, neuroanatomy, and neurophysiology, and how these principles apply to neural systems that govern processes ranging from sensation and movement to behavior and complex cognition. A special focus will be placed on understanding how neural systems are involved in neurological dysfunction and disorders. The Systems Neuroscience Major is designed to promote scholarly and professional growth. What is Systems Neuroscience? Systems Neuroscience is the scientific study of how the brain and nervous system operate across different levels—from molecules and cells to neural circuits, behavior, and cognition. This interdisciplinary field explores how neural systems control everything from basic sensory and motor functions to complex processes such as learning, decision-making, and emotion. These topics have been noted as ones in which students typically struggle and which commonly represent turning points in their academic careers. Given the critical significance that encouraging educational environments have in the accomplishment of student ambitions, TES is dedicated to starting this tutoring program under the direction of a prestigious office adviser. Open to everyone, the Ukrainian Student Society is not only about celebrating where we come from, but also about building friendships, sharing experiences, and supporting Ukraine together.

These mentors then go through training to teach special class periods on communication and teamwork in the College.
