The primary goal of UCSA is to enrich the understanding of Chinese and other Asian cultures among students and faculty at Penn State Commonwealth Campuses, while actively engaging members in a variety of academic, cultural, and social activities. We host cultural celebrations, academic workshops, and networking events to help Chinese and international students thrive in both their academic and social lives. UCSA is also committed to building connections with student groups nationwide, promoting cultural diversity, and strengthening collaboration across communities.

Our chapter was formerly known as the Penn State United Nations Campus Advocates, and we continue to promote the values of the UN in our community. We believe that by coming together with fellow students, we can make a positive impact on the world. We host bi-weekly meetings, intend on having UN and government speakers, and intend on attending leadership, global health, and/or environment summits.

Unity Christian Campus Ministry is a group of college students who want to live for God in community. We live life together and commune for Bible Studies, kickbacks, community service, and more. Our advisors are sources of spiritual, physical, and emotional support and guide us through thick and thin. As always, but especially today, UCCM is not in agreement with the mistreatment of anyone based on race, gender, religion, sexuality, and anything else of the like. Together we can live the purpose-filled life God has called us to.

Some Key Functions Include: Advocacy: UPUA represents students' concerns on issues like tuition, mental health, DEI, sustainability, and academic policies. Programming: They host events, initiatives, and services such as free test-prep books, airport shuttles, and voter registration drives. Policy Work: UPUA drafts and passes legislation that can influence university decision-making and initiate campus-wide change. Leadership: It is led by an elected President and Vice President, with an assembly made up of college representatives, at-large members, community/identity seats, and five committees. Our chapter prioritizes engaging the local community through STEM outreach, such as our own widely recognized event, STEM Rotor Day. As a group we organize trips to various rotorcraft museums and companies in vertical flight such as Boeing and Sikorsky.

In order to become a member, you must attend a placement class at the beginning of the semester so we can place you in the correct level. This is not an audition, but to simply gauge your technical skills. We offer three levels of technique classes: beginner, intermediate, and advanced. We also offer skills & strengths conditioning classes. As a performer, you must attend one of these classes a week, plus one hour of rehearsal per each showcase dance you are in. We perform all around Penn State's campus, most notably at THON and PSU's Best Dance Crew. We believe running is more than a sport, it's a tool for connection, self-growth, and social impact. Open to runners of all backgrounds, identities, and fitness levels, our club creates a welcoming space where everyone belongs, whether you're sprinting, jogging, or walking. Our weekly meetups include conversational-paced runs, themed events like our "Halloween Run" and "Single's Run Night" as well as monthly explorations of new routes around State College. But we don't stop at the finish line. We host socials, and cultural awareness events, volunteer at local races, and partner with other student orgs to uplift diverse voices. Our initiatives like "Running with a Purpose" shine a light on issues that matter, making each mile meaningful. Led by a passionate board of student leaders, We Are Runners is committed to fostering a supportive community that values health, inclusion, friendship, and action. Whether you're looking to train, find your people, or make a difference, there's a place for you here.

Our goal is to provide a community for our members to learn about horses, improve their riding skills, and compete on an intercollegiate level. Through competitions hosted by the Intercollegiate Horse Show Association (IHSA) our members, from beginners to long-time horsemen, can compete in horsemanship, ranch riding, and reining classes depending on their skill levels. clubs.summary: Whiplash is an organization of fun, yet committed dancers with a strong passion for dance. Priding ourselves on doing what we love, we are heavily involved in Penn State activities such as homecoming and Penn State Dance Marathon (THON).

Our goal as a group is to promote the development of all phases of wildlife research and management along sound biological lines, in addition to connecting individuals to professionals in the field and the wildlife that surrounds us. Some of our events include Kids Go Wild (an outreach event to educate kids on wildlife science), talks from professionals in the industry, and other cool activities and workshops! clubs.name: Wind Energy Club at University Park
clubs.summary: We are a multidisciplinary organization that competes in the the DOE's annual Collegiate Wind Competition! If you are looking to gain hands-on business, engineering, or outreach experience, the Wind Energy Club is the perfect place for you :)
clubs.description: !!Join our Teams page and sign-up for our email newsletter!! The Department of Energy (DOE) Collegiate Wind Competition (CWC) prepares you to enter the the wind and renewable energy workforce. CWC is divided into three main contests: Turbine Prototype, Project Development, and Connection Creation. The Turbine Prototype contest challenges you to design and build a small-scale off-shore wind turbine. The turbine must then complete a set of tasks in a wind tunnel at the in-person competition. Through the Project Development contest, you will design a hypothetical wind farm project from scratch. You will also learn about site planning, financial planning, risk, environmental, and societal analysis, and more. The Connection Creation contest allows you to gain stronger marketing and outreach skills through social media management, event planning, and community engagement. We have won first place in the CWC 5 times since its inaugural competition in 2014. We hope that you will join us to continue that legacy!

clubs.description: What kind of men are we? Zeta Psi is a historic, elite, and intimate brotherhood. Since 1847, we have taken pride in the caliber of schools we are at and the quality of men we invite to join. Zeta Psi has active chapters at the best schools in the United States, Canada, England, Ireland, and France, and from them, recruits the finest of men — leaders, scholars, athletes, and philanthropists. A uniquely valuable sense of community stems from our intimate size that groups with 100, 200 or more chapters can't match. That sense of real brotherhood is very important to us, and it's why we have such involved, life-long alumni. What makes a Zete? Zetes come together to have fun, enjoy life, get the most out of college, better ourselves, and form lifelong bonds of brotherhood. Despite all the fun that college brings, the main reason you came to school is to get an education with the hopes of that translating to success in life. All our brothers can attest that you get more than the necessary knowledge, experience, and skill from Zeta Psi. Our goal, and the reason we exist, is to help you succeed by graduating with that edge you need in life. The result: better and more successful men
